The program brokers agreements, provides standards and orientation to ensure spaces are safe and move-in ready, and offers ongoing support to both hosts and renters to keep placements stable.

name: Acadia Homestay (English Language Centre)

solution_text: Vacant Property Activation and Matchmaking: Create a volunteer-run inventory of vacant homes/units and broker short- or long-term matches between owners and young renters or recent returnees, combined with small rehab teams to make units move-in ready.

description: Treehouse Village is a resident-developed cohousing community where households own their individual homes and co-own extensive common facilities through a condominium corporation. description: AVRCE SchoolsPlus coordinates school-based teams—facilitators, outreach workers, and partnered mental health clinicians—embedded across Annapolis Valley schools to provide on-site counselling and social supports. The program focuses on early identification and intervention, reducing wait times by meeting students where they are and linking families to Nova Scotia Health and local community services. Integrated case planning and warm handoffs ensure youth receive the right support at the right time.
obstacle_title: Primary Care and Mental Health Gaps
solution_text: Integrated School-Based Mental Health Teams: Work with school boards to place counsellors, social workers and family clinicians in schools to provide quick access for youth, early intervention, and seamless links to community services.

name: Indigenous Health Program
description: IWK Health’s Indigenous Health Program supports Indigenous children, youth, and families through Indigenous Patient Navigators and access to traditional healing practices (e.g., smudging, ceremony) within the hospital and community. The program maintains formal partnerships with Mi’kmaw Elders and cultural service providers to integrate cultural safety and traditional wellness alongside clinical mental health care, improving timely, culturally grounded support.
obstacle_title: Primary Care and Mental Health Gaps
solution_text: Cultural and Indigenous Healing Partnerships: Develop formal partnerships with Indigenous healers and cultural service providers to offer culturally safe mental health programming and broaden the types of supports available locally.

name: Elders in Residence Program
description: Dalhousie’s Elders in Residence Program connects Indigenous students with Mi’kmaw and other Indigenous Elders for one-on-one support, sharing circles, cultural teachings, and care navigation. Through formal partnerships with Knowledge Keepers and cultural practitioners, the university offers culturally safe mental wellness supports that complement conventional counselling and reduce barriers to accessing help.
obstacle_title: Primary Care and Mental Health Gaps
solution_text: Cultural and Indigenous Healing Partnerships: Develop formal partnerships with Indigenous healers and cultural service providers to offer culturally safe mental health programming and broaden the types of supports available locally.

name: Unama’ki College Elders in Residence and Indigenous Student Support
description: Unama’ki College at Cape Breton University provides Elders-in-Residence, sharing circles, language and culture-based wellness activities, and ceremonial supports for Indigenous students. These services are delivered through formal relationships with local Mi’kmaw Elders and cultural service providers, embedding traditional healing alongside counselling to expand culturally safe mental health supports on campus and in the local community.
address: 1250 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1P 6L2
obstacle_title: Primary Care and Mental Health Gaps
solution_text: Cultural and Indigenous Healing Partnerships: Develop formal partnerships with Indigenous healers and cultural service providers to offer culturally safe mental health programming and broaden the types of supports available locally.

name: Friendly Calls (Nova Scotia)
description: The Canadian Red Cross Friendly Calls program uses a roster of trained volunteers to provide regular phone-based wellness checks, psychosocial first aid, and referrals to community and health resources. By offering immediate, short-term supportive contact—often from experienced volunteers—it helps buffer isolation and mental health strain while clients wait for permanent primary care or counselling providers.
obstacle_title: Primary Care and Mental Health Gaps
solution_text: Rapid Volunteer Roster for Crisis Coverage: Create a trained volunteer roster (retired nurses, counsellors, social workers) who can provide short-term coverage and crisis response while clients wait for permanent providers.

name: Victim Services Unit
description: Halifax Regional Police’s Victim Services Unit deploys trained volunteer responders who provide immediate crisis intervention, safety planning, and short-term emotional support to victims of crime and trauma. This rapid volunteer roster offers stabilization and navigation to health and mental health resources, bridging the gap until clients can access ongoing services such as family physicians, counsellors, or social workers.
obstacle_title: Primary Care and Mental Health Gaps
solution_text: Rapid Volunteer Roster for Crisis Coverage: Create a trained volunteer roster (retired nurses, counsellors, social workers) who can provide short-term coverage and crisis response while clients wait for permanent providers.

organization: Nova Scotia Department of Health and Wellness — Office of Healthcare Professionals Recruitment

The team organizes site visits, provides relocation incentives, and connects candidates and their partners to housing options, schools, and spousal employment supports in collaboration with municipal and community partners.

description: Nova Scotia Health’s provincial recruitment program actively attracts family physicians and nurse practitioners with relocation assistance, signing incentives, and a dedicated recruitment team. solution_text: Community Provider Recruitment Campaign: Coordinate a local recruitment package promoting quality of life, housing support, spousal employment help, and relocation bonuses to attract family doctors, nurse practitioners and therapists to the area.

name: Laing House (Youth Peer Support Centre)
description: Laing House is a youth-driven, non-clinical drop-in centre for people aged 16–29 living with mental illness. It offers daily peer support check-ins and group programs such as art, music, life skills, and mindfulness that build coping and social connection. Staff and peer leaders also help members navigate and connect to primary care and community mental health services, reducing wait-time barriers in a welcoming, stigma-free setting.
obstacle_title: Primary Care and Mental Health Gaps
solution_text: Wellness Hubs and Drop-in Centres: Open community wellness hubs offering daytime drop-in mental health check-ins, group programs (art, job skills, mindfulness), and connections to primary care referrals in a non-clinical setting.

name: The North Grove Community Hub
description: The North Grove operates a welcoming, non-clinical community hub with drop-in resource navigation and supportive check-ins through on-site staff and social workers. It offers group programs that foster wellness and life skills—such as community kitchens, gardening, parenting support, and peer groups—and regularly partners with local services to link residents to primary care and mental health supports. This approach reduces barriers to care while building community connection and resilience.
obstacle_title: Primary Care and Mental Health Gaps
solution_text: Wellness Hubs and Drop-in Centres: Open community wellness hubs offering daytime drop-in mental health check-ins, group programs (art, job skills, mindfulness), and connections to primary care referrals in a non-clinical setting.

name: Ally Centre of Cape Breton – Drop-in & Wellness Programs
description: The Ally Centre runs a harm reduction–focused, non-judgmental drop-in space offering daily wellness check-ins, outreach nursing, and peer support. It provides group programming (health education, life skills, and peer groups) and actively connects people to primary care and mental health services through referrals and accompaniment. The centre functions as a community wellness hub that lowers access barriers for those facing long wait times or limited provider availability.
obstacle_title: Primary Care and Mental Health Gaps
solution_text: Wellness Hubs and Drop-in Centres: Open community wellness hubs offering daytime drop-in mental health check-ins, group programs (art, job skills, mindfulness), and connections to primary care referrals in a non-clinical setting.

name: MusGo Rider Co-operative Ltd.
description: MusGo Rider is a member-governed transportation co-operative serving the Eastern Shore of Halifax Regional Municipality, running scheduled shuttle runs and pre-booked services that connect coastal communities with town centers, services, and jobs. As a co-op, local members help set fares, plan routes, and support operations, using community-owned/leased vans and rotating staff/volunteers to keep costs affordable and services responsive.
solution_text: Community Shuttle Cooperative: A locally governed cooperative that runs scheduled shuttles between villages, town centers and employment hubs using community-owned or leased minibuses. Members help plan routes, manage operations, set fares and rotate driving/administrative duties to keep costs low and responsive to local needs.

name: Colchester Transportation Cooperative Limited (CTCL)
description: CTCL is a community transportation co-operative that links rural Colchester County residents with Truro and nearby service and employment centres through scheduled shuttles and coordinated trips. Member representation on its board guides fare policy and service design, and the co-op model enables community-driven route planning and shared operations using minibuses and vans.

name: Wheels of Hope (Transportation Services) – Nova Scotia
organization: Canadian Cancer Society – The Lodge That Gives
description: Wheels of Hope coordinates screened volunteer drivers to provide door-to-door rides for people undergoing cancer treatment across Nova Scotia, covering trips that public transit often cannot, such as early-morning or out-of-town medical appointments. Volunteers use their own vehicles, scheduling is arranged through the program, and mileage/expense supports are provided so service remains affordable and reliable for clients.
solution_text: Volunteer Driver Network: A coordinated volunteer program where screened community volunteers provide rides for seniors, jobseekers, students and shift workers for trips that public transit doesn't serve (early/late shifts, medical appointments, interviews). name: Volunteer Transportation Program – Annapolis Valley
description: VON’s Volunteer Transportation Program recruits and screens community volunteers to drive clients to essential appointments and errands when other transportation options are limited, especially in rural communities. name: E-Bike Lending Library
organization: Municipality of the County of Kings — Recreation Services
description: The Municipality of the County of Kings operates a no-cost e-bike lending library that allows residents to borrow electric-assist bicycles and accessories for several days at a time. The program provides basic safety orientation and route-planning support so people can try short trips, commutes, and errands without a car, particularly in rural areas with limited transit. By removing upfront cost barriers and including gear like helmets and bike bags, it functions as a community bike library aligned with last-mile mobility goals.

Staff provide an introduction to e-bike operation, charging, and basic maintenance, enabling people to replace short car trips and connect to work or services where transit is sparse. The program supports low-barrier access by offering free loans and outreach to communities across the district.

name: SmartTrip Halifax (Employer Commuter Options Program)
description: SmartTrip is Halifax Regional Municipality’s employer-focused travel demand management program that helps workplaces develop commuter plans, coordinate staggered shifts, and run carpool/vanpool matching and incentive campaigns. The program partners with employers, post-secondary institutions, and community groups to implement ride-pooling, promote transit, and connect staff to benefits like EPass and Emergency Ride Home—reducing single-occupant trips to major job centres. SmartTrip provides resources, data, and engagement support so employers and local councils can collaboratively deliver shared commuter solutions.
solution_text: Employer‑Community Commuter Partnerships: Local employers, town councils and community groups collaborate to create shared commuter solutions: pooled shuttles to industrial parks, staggered shift coordination, employer-provided transit subsidies, and ride-pooling incentives to reduce single-occupant car trips.

name: CarShare Atlantic for Business (Corporate Membership)
description: CarShare Atlantic partners with employers and institutions across Halifax to offer corporate carshare memberships and on-site vehicles so staff can commute by transit, shuttle, or carpool and still access a car for work trips. This arrangement helps employers reduce parking demand and single-occupant commuting by enabling shared commuting to the workplace and shifting necessary daytime travel to a pooled fleet. Employers often combine the corporate plan with transit subsidies and ride-pooling incentives to support a comprehensive shared-commuter strategy.

solution_text: Employer‑Community Commuter Partnerships: Local employers, town councils and community groups collaborate to create shared commuter solutions: pooled shuttles to industrial parks, staggered shift coordination, employer-provided transit subsidies, and ride-pooling incentives to reduce single-occupant car trips.

name: Bridge Terminal (Mobility Hub)
description: Halifax Transit’s Bridge Terminal is a major mobility hub where numerous urban and suburban routes converge, providing heated indoor waiting areas, accessible shelters, bike racks, and real-time digital departure displays with clear wayfinding signage. The terminal is adjacent to ride-hail/taxi pick-up zones and local active transportation connections, making transfers safer and quicker for regional commuters. By concentrating services and amenities in one place, it functions as a practical mobility hub that eases first/last-mile connections.

This layout reduces car dependence by making transfers to Halifax more convenient and safe.

name: PC Connect Special Event and Weekend Service
organization: Municipality of Pictou County (PC Connect Rural Transit)

On weekends and event days, these buses act as community shuttles linking Pictou, New Glasgow, Stellarton, Westville, and Trenton so residents, students, and visitors can get to activities without a car. By filling mobility gaps when intercity options are limited, the service demonstrates demand for more frequent regional transit.
solution_text: Intercommunity Weekend/Seasonal Shuttle: Community-organized weekend or seasonal intercity shuttle service (farm markets, festivals, student travel, regional job fairs) that fills gaps left by infrequent intercity routes and demonstrates demand for more regular service.

name: Maritime Bus Acadia University Connector
description: Maritime Bus runs semester-timed Friday/Sunday and holiday shuttles during the academic year between Wolfville (Acadia University) and Halifax/Halifax Stanfield International Airport to match peak student travel. This targeted, seasonal schedule supplements the regular intercity network and provides reliable weekend mobility for youth and students without cars. By aggregating demand around weekends and breaks, the connector illustrates the viability of sustained intercommunity service between the Annapolis Valley and Halifax.
solution_text: Intercommunity Weekend/Seasonal Shuttle: Community-organized weekend or seasonal intercity shuttle service (farm markets, festivals, student travel, regional job fairs) that fills gaps left by infrequent intercity routes and demonstrates demand for more regular service.

These public insights help governments and service providers identify access gaps for equity-deserving populations—including newcomers, 2SLGBTQIA+ communities, and people with disabilities—while adhering to strict consent and privacy safeguards.
solution_text: Community Data and Progress Dashboard: Co-create, with consent and privacy safeguards, a public dashboard tracking equity indicators (employment, wages, housing, service access) for Mi'kmaq, African Nova Scotians, newcomers, 2SLGBTQIA+, and people with disabilities to guide policy and accountability.

name: Equity and Anti-Racism Data and Progress Reporting
organization: Government of Nova Scotia – Office of Equity and Anti-Racism Initiatives
description: The Office of Equity and Anti-Racism Initiatives coordinates the collection and governance of disaggregated equity data across the provincial government and publishes public-facing progress reporting tied to Nova Scotia’s equity and anti-racism priorities. This work advances a cross-government dashboard approach to track outcomes in employment, income, housing, and service access for Mi’kmaq communities, African Nova Scotians, newcomers, 2SLGBTQIA+ people, and persons with disabilities, with strong consent, privacy, and community oversight practices.
solution_text: Community Data and Progress Dashboard: Co-create, with consent and privacy safeguards, a public dashboard tracking equity indicators (employment, wages, housing, service access) for Mi'kmaq, African Nova Scotians, newcomers, 2SLGBTQIA+, and people with disabilities to guide policy and accountability.

name: Spryfield Family Medicine Teaching Site – After-Hours Clinic
description: Dalhousie Family Medicine’s Spryfield teaching clinic runs after-hours primary care sessions for its community and rostered patients, scheduling evening and select weekend appointments outside the regular workday. Services are provided by rotating family medicine residents and supervising physicians, with nurse practitioners involved, enabling both same-day/urgent bookings and short walk-in windows that improve timely access for working-age and youth patients.
obstacle_title: Health Care and Mental Health Access Shortfalls
solution_text: Community-run evening and weekend primary care clinics: Local clinics staffed by rotating volunteer family doctors, nurse practitioners and medical students to provide walk-in and booked appointments outside typical hours, reducing wait times and improving access for working youth.

name: Family Focus Medical Clinics – After-Hours and Walk‑In Care
description: Family Focus Medical Clinics provide extended evening and weekend primary care through a combination of booked and walk-in visits, allowing working youth and adults to access care beyond typical office hours. Clinics are staffed by rotating family physicians and nurse practitioners across multiple sites, which helps reduce wait times for non-urgent issues and diverts patients from emergency departments.
obstacle_title: Health Care and Mental Health Access Shortfalls
solution_text: Community-run evening and weekend primary care clinics: Local clinics staffed by rotating volunteer family doctors, nurse practitioners and medical students to provide walk-in and booked appointments outside typical hours, reducing wait times and improving access for working youth.

name: Peer Support and Mentoring Program
description: Eating Disorders Nova Scotia offers free peer-led support groups, drop-ins, and one-to-one mentoring for youth and young adults, delivered by trained supporters with lived experience. The program partners with clinicians and programs at the IWK Health Centre and Nova Scotia Health for training, consultation, and coordinated care, providing warm referrals to clinical services when needed. By centering lived experience in welcoming spaces, it reduces stigma and helps youth navigate services early.
address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 309, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2
obstacle_title: Health Care and Mental Health Access Shortfalls
solution_text: Peer-led youth mental health networks: Trained peer supporters and drop-in groups run by young people in collaboration with clinicians to provide early support, navigation, destigmatized conversation spaces and warm referrals to clinical services.

name: Youth Peer Support (Mental Health & Addictions)
description: IWK Health integrates Youth Peer Support Specialists with lived experience into its Mental Health & Addictions services for adolescents and young adults. These peers co-facilitate groups and offer one-to-one support, helping youth navigate services and providing warm hand-offs to clinicians within IWK and to community partners. The model fosters early engagement, destigmatized conversations, and better connections to appropriate clinical care.
obstacle_title: Health Care and Mental Health Access Shortfalls
solution_text: Peer-led youth mental health networks: Trained peer supporters and drop-in groups run by young people in collaboration with clinicians to provide early support, navigation, destigmatized conversation spaces and warm referrals to clinical services.

name: SchoolsPlus (School-Based Integrated Services)
organization: Nova Scotia Department of Education and Early Childhood Development
description: SchoolsPlus embeds multidisciplinary teams—including SchoolsPlus facilitators, social workers, mental health clinicians and community partners—directly in public schools across Nova Scotia. These teams provide on-site assessment, brief counselling/therapeutic intervention and coordinated referrals, and they help students access virtual care from school when needed, reducing wait times and barriers to service while keeping youth in their learning environments.
obstacle_title: Health Care and Mental Health Access Shortfalls
solution_text: School- and campus-based mental health teams: Embed social workers, counsellors and telehealth pods in schools and post-secondary campuses so students get timely assessment, brief therapy and referral without leaving education settings.

name: Dalhousie Student Health & Wellness – Counselling & Psychological Services
description: Dalhousie embeds counsellors, social workers and a stepped-care mental health team on campus to provide same-day/single-session counselling, brief therapy and coordinated referrals to community/psychiatric care as needed. Services are offered in-person and virtually, with private on-campus spaces available for telehealth appointments so students can access care without leaving the university setting.
obstacle_title: Health Care and Mental Health Access Shortfalls
solution_text: School- and campus-based mental health teams: Embed social workers, counsellors and telehealth pods in schools and post-secondary campuses so students get timely assessment, brief therapy and referral without leaving education settings.

name: NSCC Ivany Campus Counselling Services
organization: Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) – Ivany Campus
description: Nova Scotia Community College provides on-campus counselling at the Ivany Campus, embedding counsellors within Student Services to deliver timely intake, brief therapy, crisis support and referrals to Nova Scotia Health or community providers. The service offers flexible access through in-person and virtual appointments, with private rooms available on campus for students who need a confidential space for telehealth sessions.
obstacle_title: Health Care and Mental Health Access Shortfalls
solution_text: School- and campus-based mental health teams: Embed social workers, counsellors and telehealth pods in schools and post-secondary campuses so students get timely assessment, brief therapy and referral without leaving education settings.

name: Nancy Dingwall Health and Counselling Centre – Counselling Services
description: Cape Breton University’s on-campus centre embeds a multidisciplinary team—including counsellors and health professionals—to provide mental health assessment, brief counselling and coordinated referrals for students. The centre offers both in-person and virtual counselling, enabling students to access tele-mental health from campus and receive timely support without leaving their educational environment.

solution_text: School- and campus-based mental health teams: Embed social workers, counsellors and telehealth pods in schools and post-secondary campuses so students get timely assessment, brief therapy and referral without leaving education settings.

name: Book a Room (Private Study and Meeting Rooms for Virtual Care)
description: Halifax Public Libraries offers free, bookable private rooms and study spaces with reliable high-speed internet where residents can attend virtual primary care or mental health appointments. Library staff provide basic tech help (e.g., setting up devices, using Zoom/Teams, connecting headsets) and can assist patrons in accessing Nova Scotia Health’s VirtualCareNS or other telehealth platforms, effectively functioning as community telehealth hubs.

name: Book a Room & Tech Help for Virtual Appointments
description: The Truro Library provides bookable private rooms and public computers with broadband internet to support residents who need a quiet, confidential space for virtual medical or counseling appointments. Staff offer one-on-one technology assistance to help users connect with clinicians, navigate telehealth platforms, and ensure audio/video privacy, aligning with the community telehealth hub model.
obstacle_title: Health Care and Mental Health Access Shortfalls
solution_text: Community telehealth hubs: Privacy-equipped rooms in libraries, community centres and youth hubs with high-speed internet and trained facilitators to help residents connect with virtual primary care and mental health appointments.

description: McConnell Library in Sydney offers bookable quiet rooms and computer workstations with high-speed internet where community members can attend virtual appointments with primary care providers or mental health clinicians. Staff can assist with video platform setup, device connection, and privacy accessories (e.g., headsets), making the branch a practical telehealth access point for Cape Breton residents.
obstacle_title: Health Care and Mental Health Access Shortfalls
solution_text: Community telehealth hubs: Privacy-equipped rooms in libraries, community centres and youth hubs with high-speed internet and trained facilitators to help residents connect with virtual primary care and mental health appointments.

name: Mainline Mobile Outreach (Needle Exchange Van)
description: Mainline’s mobile outreach van follows regular routes across Halifax to reach people who use substances and others facing barriers to care. Staff distribute safer-use and harm-reduction supplies and naloxone, offer brief counselling and health education, and assist with referrals and appointment booking for detox, opioid agonist treatment, testing, and primary care.
obstacle_title: Health Care and Mental Health Access Shortfalls
solution_text: Mobile health and mental health outreach units: Regularly scheduled vans or pop-up clinics that visit rural and underserved neighbourhoods to deliver primary care, counselling, harm reduction supplies and appointment booking support.

name: Ally Centre Street Outreach and Mobile Harm Reduction
description: The Ally Centre operates street outreach and a mobile harm-reduction service throughout the Cape Breton Regional Municipality, including rural and underserved areas. The team distributes sterile equipment and naloxone, provides brief counselling and peer support, and connects clients to testing, addictions care, and primary care by arranging referrals and appointments; a street nurse offers basic primary care and wound care during pop-up visits.
obstacle_title: Health Care and Mental Health Access Shortfalls
solution_text: Mobile health and mental health outreach units: Regularly scheduled vans or pop-up clinics that visit rural and underserved neighbourhoods to deliver primary care, counselling, harm reduction supplies and appointment booking support.

name: Mental Health Mobile Crisis Team (HRM)
organization: IWK Health and Nova Scotia Health
description: The Mental Health Mobile Crisis Team provides 24/7 telephone triage and mobile mental health outreach in Halifax Regional Municipality. Clinicians travel to homes and community locations to deliver on-site assessment, brief counselling, and safety planning, and they connect clients to ongoing services by coordinating referrals and follow-up appointments with community mental health and addictions programs.
obstacle_title: Health Care and Mental Health Access Shortfalls
solution_text: Mobile health and mental health outreach units: Regularly scheduled vans or pop-up clinics that visit rural and underserved neighbourhoods to deliver primary care, counselling, harm reduction supplies and appointment booking support.

name: Antigonish Physician Recruitment Committee
description: Hosted by the St. Martha’s Regional Hospital Foundation, this community-led committee partners with the Town and County of Antigonish, local employers, and Nova Scotia Health to recruit and retain physicians. It organizes customized community tours, helps with relocation and housing, facilitates spousal employment and school placements, and connects newcomers with local clinical mentors and social networks. These locally tailored incentive packages support long‑term retention and expand access to primary and mental health care in the region.
obstacle_title: Health Care and Mental Health Access Shortfalls
solution_text: Local clinician recruitment and retention partnerships: Community-driven incentive packages (mentorship, subsidized housing, relocation supports, integration into local social networks) developed with municipal and business partners to attract and keep providers.

name: Town of Lunenburg Physician Recruitment Initiative
description: The Town of Lunenburg collaborates with local businesses, housing providers, and health-system partners to attract family physicians and other clinicians to the community. The initiative offers municipal incentive supports, assists with housing searches and relocation logistics, and connects providers and their families to community ambassadors, clubs, and social networks; it also facilitates mentorship linkages with local practitioners. These community-driven packages help new clinicians settle and stay, improving access to primary and mental health services on the South Shore.
obstacle_title: Health Care and Mental Health Access Shortfalls
solution_text: Local clinician recruitment and retention partnerships: Community-driven incentive packages (mentorship, subsidized housing, relocation supports, integration into local social networks) developed with municipal and business partners to attract and keep providers.

name: Clare Health Centre (Centre de santé de Clare)
organization: Municipality of the District of Clare
description: A municipally owned, community-directed primary care clinic that recruits and supports family physicians and nurse practitioners working in a collaborative practice with sustainable schedules. It improves access for rural and francophone residents (including youth and families) by offering team-based primary care, chronic disease management, and navigation to mental health/addictions services in partnership with local providers.
obstacle_title: Health Care and Mental Health Access Shortfalls
solution_text: Primary care cooperative (community-owned clinic): A community-governed clinic model that hires NPs and physicians on sustainable schedules, offers team-based care and prioritizes access for youth and underserved populations.

name: Halifax Newcomer Health Clinic
description: A team-based primary care clinic that employs physicians, nurse practitioners, nurses, and social workers to provide initial primary care and mental health supports to government-assisted refugees and other newcomers, with interpretation and trauma-informed services. It prioritizes access for an underserved population and transitions patients to long-term community practices, demonstrating sustainable, collaborative primary care scheduling and wraparound support.
address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2059, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

solution_text: Primary care cooperative (community-owned clinic): A community-governed clinic model that hires NPs and physicians on sustainable schedules, offers team-based care and prioritizes access for youth and underserved populations.

name: EHS Palliative Care Paramedic Program
organization: Emergency Health Services (EHS) Nova Scotia / Medavie Health Services Nova Scotia
description: Specially trained paramedics make home visits to people with serious illness or enrolled in palliative care, providing symptom control (e.g., pain, breathlessness), anticipatory guidance, and after-hours support using individualized care plans developed with palliative and primary care teams. Visits include caregiver coaching, medication adjustments per protocol, and screening for distress or mental health needs with connection to grief and family/youth supports as appropriate. This delivers high-quality care at home, reduces emergency department use, and strengthens continuous, person-centered care.
obstacle_title: Health Care and Mental Health Access Shortfalls
solution_text: Community paramedicine and home visit program: Expanded paramedic roles to provide in-home follow-up, chronic disease management and mental health checks, reducing ED visits and supporting continuity of care for vulnerable youth.

name: Suicide Prevention Gatekeeper Training (safeTALK and ASIST)
organization: Nova Scotia Health, Mental Health and Addictions Program
description: Nova Scotia Health’s Mental Health and Addictions Program partners with community organizations to deliver safeTALK and ASIST suicide-prevention training across the province, often at no or low cost. These certified courses prepare teachers, coaches, employers, faith leaders and volunteers to recognize suicide risk, engage safely, and make timely referrals to crisis lines and local mental health services.
obstacle_title: Health Care and Mental Health Access Shortfalls
solution_text: Mental Health First Aid and suicide prevention training: Free or low-cost certified training for teachers, coaches, employers, faith leaders and volunteers so more community members can recognize crisis signs and make timely referrals.

name: Teacher Mental Health First Aid and Suicide Prevention PD
description: The Nova Scotia Teachers Union provides professional development that includes Mental Health First Aid and suicide-prevention sessions (e.g., safeTALK) for teachers and school staff across the province. These trainings build educators’ capacity to notice warning signs in students and colleagues, have supportive conversations, and make timely referrals to school-based and provincial mental health services.
address: 3106 Joseph Howe Drive, Halifax, NS B3L 4L7
obstacle_title: Health Care and Mental Health Access Shortfalls
solution_text: Mental Health First Aid and suicide prevention training: Free or low-cost certified training for teachers, coaches, employers, faith leaders and volunteers so more community members can recognize crisis signs and make timely referrals.

name: CBI Health Return-to-Work and Mental Health Services (Halifax)
description: CBI Health partners with local employers to deliver occupational rehabilitation and mental health supports that help employees, including young workers, access counselling and structured return-to-work plans. Services are offered in-person and virtually, and include coordination with employers for flexible scheduling, workplace accommodations, and graduated return-to-work after mental health leave. CBI clinicians also liaise with primary care and EAP providers to ensure seamless care between the workplace and community services.
obstacle_title: Health Care and Mental Health Access Shortfalls
solution_text: Employer-community youth wellness partnerships: Local employers partner with clinics and counselling services to offer flexible scheduling, on-site or virtual counselling access, employee assistance for young workers and supported return-to-work plans.

name: Sharp Advice Needle Exchange
description: Sharp Advice provides low‑barrier harm reduction services including distribution of sterile supplies, take‑home naloxone kits, and safer‑use education. Peer outreach workers with lived experience offer nonjudgmental support and navigation, helping people connect to detox, opioid agonist treatment, and mental health and social services, reducing barriers to care for youth and adults.
obstacle_title: Health Care and Mental Health Access Shortfalls

name: Needle Distribution & Harm Reduction Program
description: Northern Healthy Connections Society operates a community harm reduction site that distributes sterile equipment, provides take‑home naloxone kits and training, and offers safer‑use information. Peer outreach workers build trust, provide nonjudgmental support, and navigate clients to addiction treatment, primary care, and mental health services across Colchester and surrounding areas.
obstacle_title: Health Care and Mental Health Access Shortfalls
solution_text: Harm reduction and addiction peer navigation services: Peer navigators and community harm reduction sites that distribute naloxone, provide safer-use information, linkage to treatment and nonjudgmental support to reduce barriers into care.

description: Direction 180 provides low‑threshold opioid agonist treatment and harm reduction services, including naloxone distribution, safer‑use education, and mobile/community outreach that meets people where they are. Peer and outreach staff offer nonjudgmental support and practical navigation—assisting with appointments, referrals, and linkage to broader health and social services to reduce barriers into care.

solution_text: Harm reduction and addiction peer navigation services: Peer navigators and community harm reduction sites that distribute naloxone, provide safer-use information, linkage to treatment and nonjudgmental support to reduce barriers into care.

organization: Nova Scotia Health – Indigenous Health Program
description: Nova Scotia Health’s Indigenous Patient Navigation Services provide Indigenous youth and families with culturally safe support across the care journey, including advocacy, care coordination, and links to Elders and traditional healing. Navigators help youth access mental health and addictions services more effectively by bridging cultural gaps and addressing systemic barriers.

solution_text: Culturally safe and Indigenous-led services: Support Indigenous and newcomer-led counselling, traditional healing programs and multilingual navigators to ensure services are welcoming and effective for diverse youth.

name: Settlement Services
description: YWCA Halifax’s Settlement Services provide trauma-informed counselling, case management, and referrals for newcomer women and youth, with access to interpretation and multilingual navigation. The program supports mental wellness by offering culturally responsive, gender-informed services that help youth connect to the right health and social supports quickly.
address: 358 Herring Cove Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3R 1V8

solution_text: Culturally safe and Indigenous-led services: Support Indigenous and newcomer-led counselling, traditional healing programs and multilingual navigators to ensure services are welcoming and effective for diverse youth.

name: Transport de Clare – Community Transportation
description: Transport de Clare offers pre-booked, door-to-door rides across the Municipality of Clare, using community drivers and accessible vehicles to get residents to health clinics, counselling, and follow-up appointments. With affordable, subsidized fares and scheduled routes when demand warrants, it functions as a community-run alternative to ride-share for rural youth and families who lack reliable transportation.
obstacle_title: Health Care and Mental Health Access Shortfalls
solution_text: Volunteer ride-share and transit voucher programs: Community-run transportation assistance (volunteer drivers, subsidy vouchers, scheduled shuttle routes) so young people can reliably reach clinics, counselling and follow-ups.

name: Chebucto Connections

The Pathways to Education program provides mentoring, tutoring, and career exploration, and staff connect youth to Nova Scotia Works job services and host skill-building workshops. The hub also offers community arts and recreation activities and helps residents access primary care and mental health resources, reducing barriers and wait-time impacts.

name: Wolfville Children’s Centre
description: A community-founded, parent-governed non-profit that operates a licensed early learning and child care centre offering infant, toddler, preschool, and school-age care in a small, neighbourhood setting. Parents serve on the board and lead fundraising and volunteer efforts, pooling time and local resources to expand spaces and keep costs manageable—directly reflecting the co-operative, community-owned micro-centre model described.
obstacle_title: Childcare Availability and Early Learning Workforce
solution_text: Community Childcare Co-ops: Parent-led cooperatives that pool time, skills and small local funding to open and run licensed micro-centres in towns and neighbourhoods, reducing costs and increasing local ownership.

name: Lunenburg Day Care Centre
description: A parent- and community-led non-profit society that runs a licensed early learning centre in the Town of Lunenburg, offering small-group childcare close to where families live and work. Families participate in governance, volunteering, and local fundraising to support staffing and facilities—embodying a cooperative, community-owned approach that lowers barriers and sustains a micro-centre in a rural setting.

solution_text: Community Childcare Co-ops: Parent-led cooperatives that pool time, skills and small local funding to open and run licensed micro-centres in towns and neighbourhoods, reducing costs and increasing local ownership.

description: The YMCA of Southwest Nova Scotia operates school-based before- and after-school programs in partnership with elementary schools across Yarmouth, Digby, and Shelburne counties. Utilizing classrooms and gym spaces, the program offers affordable, licensed care that aligns with school schedules and supports parents working standard and extended hours.
obstacle_title: Childcare Availability and Early Learning Workforce
solution_text: School-based Before/After Programs: Use elementary school classrooms and gyms to host affordable before- and after-school care, coordinated by community organizations and municipal recreation departments.

description: Université Sainte-Anne offers a French-language ECE diploma tailored to Acadian and Francophone communities, combining online learning with work-integrated placements in local centres. name: Kijiji Halifax – Childcare & Nanny Share Listings
description: Kijiji’s Halifax Childcare category is actively used by local parents to create and join neighborhood nanny shares, enabling families to pool resources and arrange shared caregivers for split shifts and off-peak hours. Listings and location filters help match nearby households and caregivers, while built-in messaging supports parent-run scheduling and coordination for flexible, non-standard care arrangements across the HRM and surrounding areas.

Many clubs run pitch nights or provide small startup budgets, giving practical experience, mentorship from volunteer leaders, and early revenue opportunities that build an entrepreneurial mindset from a young age.
address: 60 Research Drive, Bible Hill, NS B6L 2R2
solution_text: Youth Entrepreneurship Pipeline: School and community programs that teach business basics, run micro-grants and summer incubators for teens and young adults to build experience, networks and a culture of local entrepreneurship from an early age.

name: Matched Community Impact Campaigns
description: United Way Halifax runs targeted, crowdfunding-style campaigns that pool small resident donations through their online giving pages and CanadaHelps project pages. Corporate and foundation partners frequently provide time-limited matching funds, doubling community contributions to priority initiatives focused on poverty reduction, youth opportunity, and equity for Black and Indigenous communities—mirroring a locally branded crowdfunding model that unlocks matching dollars for projects meeting regional goals.
solution_text: Community Crowdfunding Platform with Matching: A locally branded crowdfunding portal that aggregates small contributions from residents, paired with matching funds from local government or foundations for projects that meet regional priorities and equity goals.

name: Centre for Women in Business (CWB) – Mentorship and Growth Programs
organization: Centre for Women in Business, Mount Saint Vincent University
description: CWB at Mount Saint Vincent University offers women-led cohorts, mentorship circles, and advisory groups that provide hands-on guidance from experienced entrepreneurs and sector experts. Through tailored programming, navigation of regulations, and connections to microgrant/financing partners, CWB reduces early-stage barriers for women founders across Nova Scotia, with supports designed to reflect women’s diverse lived experiences and business contexts.
solution_text: Inclusive Entrepreneur Supports (Women, Indigenous, Newcomers): Targeted microgrants, mentorship circles, culturally appropriate programming and language supports developed with community leaders to lower barriers for historically underrepresented entrepreneurs.

name: Tech Help (One-on-One and Drop-In)
description: Halifax Public Libraries offers free one-on-one appointments and small-group workshops where staff and trained volunteers help patrons with computer and smartphone basics, email, video conferencing tools (e.g., Zoom), and cloud productivity apps. Sessions frequently support online job search and applications, resume uploading, and navigating government services such as Service Canada, CRA, and Nova Scotia online portals—directly addressing digital access barriers for residents across HRM.
address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9
solution_text: Digital Skills and Support Volunteers: Organize volunteer tutors to run free workshops and one‑on‑one sessions on basic digital literacy, remote work tools, online job search and navigating government services.

name: Digital Skills Tutoring
description: Dartmouth Learning Network provides free, volunteer-led one-on-one and small-group tutoring for adults to build essential digital skills, including computer fundamentals, email, document creation, and safe internet use. Tutors also support learners with online job search and applications, using remote work tools, and navigating government websites and digital forms—helping reduce digital barriers to employment and services.
address: 73 Tacoma Drive, Suite 802, Dartmouth, NS B2W 3Y6
solution_text: Digital Skills and Support Volunteers: Organize volunteer tutors to run free workshops and one‑on‑one sessions on basic digital literacy, remote work tools, online job search and navigating government services.

name: Pictou County Transit
organization: Town of New Glasgow (in partnership with Pictou County municipalities)
description: Pictou County Transit runs community-scale buses linking New Glasgow, Stellarton, Westville, and nearby communities to major employers, Aberdeen Hospital, retail centres, and NSCC. Its local shuttle-style routes and schedules improve access to jobs and education for youth and workers, supporting mobility where regional and intercity options are limited.
address: 111 Provost Street, New Glasgow, NS B2H 5E1
solution_text: Local Micro‑Transit and Shuttle Services: Run community‑organized shuttle routes or flexible micro‑transit (volunteer drivers, small buses or contracted vans) timed for shift work, school and major employment centres.

name: East Hants Community Rider
description: East Hants Community Rider operates a door-to-door volunteer driver program that connects residents to employment, medical appointments, training, and essential services throughout rural East Hants. Riders book trips by phone or online, and vetted volunteer drivers use their vehicles to fill gaps where fixed-route transit does not operate.
solution_text: Volunteer Ride Share Network: Set up a coordinated volunteer driving program with vetted drivers and an easy booking system to help people reach jobs, medical appointments and training when transit is limited.

name: X-Bikes (Campus Bike Share)
description: StFX’s X-Bikes is a community‑oriented bike‑share that offers students and staff free or low‑cost access to bicycles for short‑term trips around Antigonish, with secure racks and on‑campus pick‑up/return points. The Sustainability Office maintains the fleet and hosts bike safety and maintenance workshops, helping to normalize everyday cycling and support first‑/last‑mile connectivity in the town.
solution_text: Active Transportation Projects: Community‑led projects to install bike racks, repair stations, safe crosswalks and wayfinding, plus volunteer‑run bike repair clinics and local bike‑share pilots to increase cycling and walking options.

name: Chester Internet Speed Test and Broadband Gaps Map
organization: Municipality of the District of Chester
description: The Municipality of the District of Chester invites residents to complete home Internet speed tests and short surveys to gather address‑level performance data. Results are aggregated into interactive maps that reveal underserved pockets across the municipality. Chester uses these findings to prioritize underserved roads and communities for pilot builds and to support funding applications and negotiations with Internet service providers.
solution_text: Community Broadband Mapping and Needs Assessment: Collect household‑level data on connectivity through surveys and speed tests, produce maps to show gaps, and use findings to target local pilots and support funding applications.

name: WorkSpace Atlantic – Bedford Coworking
description: WorkSpace Atlantic is a local coworking provider that offers day passes, dedicated desks, private offices, and meeting rooms with high-speed Wi‑Fi in Bedford. By activating commercial space for flexible, bookable work pods and shared areas, it gives remote workers, students, and entrepreneurs reliable connectivity close to home. This advances the solution by enabling co-working use of local business space and providing community access to connectivity without long commutes.
solution_text: Partnerships with Local Businesses for Connectivity: Encourage businesses to open Wi‑Fi access or host work pods, sponsor community internet infrastructure, or allow co‑working use of underused space during off hours.

name: CBU Express and Event Overflow Shuttles
organization: Cape Breton Regional Municipality – Transit Cape Breton
description: Transit Cape Breton launched express and overflow shuttle services to Cape Breton University during peak periods and on weekends, adding buses to connect surrounding communities with the Sydney downtown core and the CBU campus. These pop-up and expanded services respond to surges tied to semesters and events, demonstrating demand for permanent evening and weekend routes that link rural areas to a major training centre and urban amenities.
solution_text: Pop‑up Transit and Weekend Routes: Pilot weekend or event‑based shuttle services connecting rural areas to downtowns, markets and training centres to demonstrate need and build ridership data for permanent service.

name: South Shore Exhibition Park-and-Ride Shuttle
description: Each summer during the South Shore Exhibition, the Town of Bridgewater coordinates free park-and-ride shuttles that move people from outlying lots into the downtown Exhibition grounds during peak evenings and weekends. This event-based service uses existing transit resources to test demand for evening and weekend mobility, connecting surrounding residential areas to the town’s main event district and informing decisions about more permanent service levels.
solution_text: Pop‑up Transit and Weekend Routes: Pilot weekend or event‑based shuttle services connecting rural areas to downtowns, markets and training centres to demonstrate need and build ridership data for permanent service.

name: Mi'kmaw Cultural Awareness Training
description: The Confederacy of Mainland Mi'kmaq offers Mi'kmaw cultural awareness and treaty education workshops for schools, municipalities, employers, and frontline service providers. Co-facilitated by Mi'kmaw Elders, knowledge keepers, and educators, the training addresses history, treaties, cultural protocols, and practical steps to create culturally safe spaces and reduce systemic bias.
address: 57 Martin Crescent, Truro Heights, NS B6L 1N7
solution_text: Community-led Cultural Safety and Anti-Racism Training: Run regular workshops co-designed and facilitated by Mi'kmaq, African Nova Scotian, newcomer and 2SLGBTQIA+ leaders for schools, employers, service providers and community groups to reduce bias, improve service delivery and build culturally safe spaces.

name: Girls Get WISE
organization: WISEatlantic (Women in Science and Engineering – Atlantic) at Mount Saint Vincent University
description: Girls Get WISE offers mentorship-rich STEM camps, workshops, and events where girls and gender-diverse youth meet and learn from women working in science, technology, engineering, and related industries in Nova Scotia. By combining hands-on activities with direct role‑model engagement, the program builds skills, confidence, and networks that guide participants toward education and careers in technology and engineering.
solution_text: Youth Mentorship and Leadership Programs: Create local mentorship networks pairing young people from target communities with mentors in trades, technology, arts, entrepreneurship and community services to build skills, networks and pathways to meaningful careers.

name: Hope Blooms Youth Leadership and Community Hub
description: Hope Blooms operates a community hub with daily after-school drop-in programming centered on an urban farm and community kitchen, offering mentorship, leadership, and entrepreneurship opportunities. Serving many African Nova Scotian and newcomer youth, the program provides culturally grounded supports, peer connection, and referrals to counselling and wraparound services through partner agencies.
solution_text: Safe and Affirming Youth Drop-in Spaces: Fund and sustain accessible drop-in centres or designated hours in existing community hubs that provide culturally informed supports, peer groups, counselling referrals and programming for Mi'kmaq, African Nova Scotian, newcomer and 2SLGBTQIA+ youth.

name: Wagmatcook Culture & Heritage Centre
description: This Mi’kmaw-led cultural centre hosts regular public events—including traditional drumming and dance demonstrations, craft workshops, language sessions, and community feasts—guided by Elders and cultural practitioners. By welcoming schools, newcomers, and neighboring African Nova Scotian groups into shared ceremonies and teachings, the Centre nurtures reconciliation, celebrates identity, and builds lasting relationships across communities.
solution_text: Community Reconciliation and Cultural Exchange Events: Host regular public events — storytelling, music, food, workshops and shared ceremonies — led by Mi'kmaq and African Nova Scotian organizers to foster understanding, celebrate identity and create personal connections between communities.

name: Millbrook Cultural & Heritage Centre (Glooscap Heritage Centre)
organization: Millbrook First Nation (Millbrook Cultural & Heritage Centre)
description: The Centre delivers Mi’kmaw cultural programming—Elder-led storytelling, traditional arts workshops, seasonal celebrations, and educational talks—open to the public throughout the year. Through collaborations with African Nova Scotian organizations and local institutions, it convenes exchange events featuring music, food, and shared teachings that strengthen reconciliation and foster personal connections and belonging among diverse communities.
solution_text: Community Reconciliation and Cultural Exchange Events: Host regular public events — storytelling, music, food, workshops and shared ceremonies — led by Mi'kmaq and African Nova Scotian organizers to foster understanding, celebrate identity and create personal connections between communities.

name: Connector Program (International/Newcomer & Recent Graduate Streams)
description: The Halifax Partnership’s Connector Program matches immigrant and international student youth with established professionals for one-on-one informational interviews, mentorship, and warm referrals that build local networks. Participants receive job-search coaching and direct employer connections across sectors, complementing language and settlement services by providing tailored, employer-linked pathways that improve retention and belonging.
address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8
solution_text: Expanded Settlement and Language Supports: Provide locally delivered language classes, job-readiness training, credential navigation help and newcomer orientation that are tailored to youth needs and connected to schools, employers and mentorship programs.

name: Newcomer Settlement & Language Services (LINC)
description: YMCA of Cape Breton provides locally delivered settlement orientation, youth activities, and federally funded LINC English classes in Sydney to help newcomer youth build language skills and navigate school and community life. Staff offer job-readiness support and connect participants with credential resources, mentors, and local employers across Cape Breton, integrating language, employment, and mentorship supports close to where youth live.
solution_text: Expanded Settlement and Language Supports: Provide locally delivered language classes, job-readiness training, credential navigation help and newcomer orientation that are tailored to youth needs and connected to schools, employers and mentorship programs.

name: Treaty Education Nova Scotia
organization: Government of Nova Scotia (Department of Education and Early Childhood Development) in partnership with Mi'kmaw Kina'matnewey
description: Treaty Education Nova Scotia integrates Mi'kmaq history, treaty relationships, language, and contemporary contributions into the P–12 curriculum across the province. Developed in partnership with Mi'kmaw Kina'matnewey, it provides lesson plans, teacher professional learning, and classroom resources used by regional centres for education to embed accurate Indigenous content and foster respect and belonging. By normalizing Mi'kmaw perspectives and countering stereotypes, the program supports safe, inclusive school climates.
solution_text: Inclusive School Curriculum and Anti-Bullying Programs: Work with school boards and community educators to incorporate Mi'kmaq and African Nova Scotian histories and contemporary contributions, and ensure 2SLGBTQIA+ inclusive materials and anti-bullying policies are taught and enforced.

name: Halifax Local Immigration Partnership – Immigrant Advisory Table
description: The Immigrant Advisory Table convenes newcomers and former refugees to provide lived-experience advice to the Halifax Local Immigration Partnership on strategies, services and funding priorities that improve immigrant settlement and inclusion. Their input informs municipal, community and employer actions that strengthen belonging and retention for diverse newcomer communities.
address: 1601 Lower Water Street, Suite 104, Halifax, NS B3J 3P6
solution_text: Community Advisory Councils with Lived-Experience Representation: Establish or expand municipal and organizational advisory councils that include youth and representatives from Mi'kmaq, African Nova Scotian, newcomer and 2SLGBTQIA+ communities to guide local planning, services and funding decisions.

name: Community Access Program and Performance Opportunities
description: The Bus Stop Theatre Co-op operates an affordable, community-run venue that prioritizes equity-seeking artists by offering subsidized space, technical support and presentation opportunities. Regular festivals and partner-led showcases provide 2SLGBTQIA+, Indigenous, African Nova Scotian and newcomer youth with platforms to perform, develop productions and earn revenue—key steps in building community-rooted cultural enterprises.
solution_text: Cultural Entrepreneurship and Arts Funding: Create micro-grants, incubators and exhibition/performance opportunities specifically for Mi'kmaq, African Nova Scotian, newcomer and 2SLGBTQIA+ youth to build small businesses, cultural enterprises and creative careers rooted in community.

name: prideHealth
organization: Nova Scotia Health and IWK Health Centre
description: prideHealth is a partnership of Nova Scotia Health and the IWK Health Centre that improves access to safe, gender‑affirming, and 2SLGBTQIA+‑competent care across Nova Scotia. It provides navigation, referrals to counselling and mental health services, and links to peer supports, using trauma‑informed and culturally responsive practices tailored to queer and trans youth.
solution_text: Culturally Informed Mental Health and Wellness Services: Develop locally accessible mental health supports that are trauma-informed and culturally specific, including peer-support groups, Indigenous healing practices, and counselling services sensitive to racialized and queer youth experiences.

name: Nova Scotia Brotherhood and Sisterhood Initiatives
description: These community‑based health programs offer culturally specific care for people of African descent, including primary care, mental health counselling, wellness groups, and peer navigation. Grounded in trauma‑informed practice and anti‑racism, they address barriers and racism‑related stress while strengthening belonging and health for African Nova Scotian youth and families.
solution_text: Culturally Informed Mental Health and Wellness Services: Develop locally accessible mental health supports that are trauma-informed and culturally specific, including peer-support groups, Indigenous healing practices, and counselling services sensitive to racialized and queer youth experiences.

name: CMM Mental Wellness Team
description: The Confederacy of Mainland Mi'kmaq’s Mental Wellness Team delivers land‑based healing, cultural programming, and clinical counselling in Mi'kmaw communities across mainland Nova Scotia. Integrating Indigenous knowledge with trauma‑informed mental health care, the team facilitates circles, ceremonies, and peer supports alongside access to clinicians, supporting Mi'kmaq youth and families’ wellness and belonging.
solution_text: Culturally Informed Mental Health and Wellness Services: Develop locally accessible mental health supports that are trauma-informed and culturally specific, including peer-support groups, Indigenous healing practices, and counselling services sensitive to racialized and queer youth experiences.

name: Welcoming Wheels
description: Welcoming Wheels equips newcomer and low-income youth and families with refurbished bicycles, helmets, locks, lights, and safe-cycling training to support everyday mobility. By providing affordable, independent transportation for commuting to school, work, and social programs, the initiative reduces transportation barriers for underserved communities and fosters belonging and participation.
solution_text: Transport and Access Solutions for Rural and Underserved Areas: Organize community ride-shares, subsidized transit passes, bike-share programs and school-to-work shuttle services to reduce isolation and increase access to education, jobs and social programs for youth across regions.

name: Millbrook Cultural & Heritage Centre
description: The Millbrook Cultural & Heritage Centre (formerly the Glooscap Heritage Centre) advances Mi'kmaw language and culture through exhibits, school programs, and community events that highlight traditional knowledge and stories. Its craft shop and cultural tourism offerings provide revenue and jobs for Mi'kmaw artists and cultural interpreters, strengthening the local cultural economy. Programming includes language content and opportunities for youth to engage with land-based cultural teachings, acknowledging Mi'kmaq leadership in heritage education.
solution_text: Support for Mi'kmaq-led Land Stewardship and Cultural Projects: Partner with local Mi'kmaq communities on stewardship, youth land-based learning, language revitalization and cultural economy projects that strengthen identity, create jobs and acknowledge Indigenous leadership in the region.

name: Employment Equity Program and Workforce Census
organization: Halifax Regional Municipality – Office of Diversity & Inclusion/ANSAIO
description: Halifax Regional Municipality runs an Employment Equity Program that uses a confidential, voluntary workforce census to collect disaggregated data on representation, retention, and workplace experience across identity groups (including Mi’kmaq, African Nova Scotians, racialized communities, newcomers, people with disabilities, and 2SLGBTQIA+). The municipality sets representation and inclusion targets, publishes workforce diversity and progress reports, and uses results to adjust recruitment, training investments, and departmental plans to improve equitable access to municipal employment and services.
solution_text: Local Equity Data, Targets and Accountability: Collect community-level data on retention, employment and service access by identity groups (with privacy safeguards), set transparent equity targets, publish progress reports and use results to guide funding and program adjustments.

name: Race-Based Data Collection in Policing
description: The Nova Scotia Human Rights Commission leads a province-mandated initiative requiring Halifax Regional Police and Halifax District RCMP to collect standardized, privacy-protected race-based data on police interactions and publish community-level reports. The project sets clear equity objectives, identifies disparities affecting African Nova Scotian and Mi’kmaw communities, and guides policy, training, and resource allocation to reduce systemic discrimination and improve accountability.
address: 5657 Spring Garden Road, Suite 305, Halifax, NS B3J 3R4
solution_text: Local Equity Data, Targets and Accountability: Collect community-level data on retention, employment and service access by identity groups (with privacy safeguards), set transparent equity targets, publish progress reports and use results to guide funding and program adjustments.

name: YMCA of Cape Breton Immigrant Services
description: YMCA of Cape Breton Immigrant Services provides one-on-one settlement and employment counselling that guides newcomers through foreign credential recognition and local licensing pathways. Staff assist with understanding regulator requirements, filling out assessment and licensure applications, and connecting clients to bridging and upgrading programs and Nova Scotia Works supports. They also facilitate referrals for credential assessments and certified document translation to meet application standards.
solution_text: Local Credential Navigation Hub: A community-run centre that helps newcomers map their foreign credentials to local requirements, provides information on licensing bodies, connects them to bridging programs, and offers application assistance and document translation referrals.

name: Valley Connector Program
description: The Valley Connector links newcomers, recent graduates, and accompanying spouses/partners with established business and community leaders who provide targeted introductions to employers and professional contacts. Through guided networking, labour‑market orientation, and curated connections, spouses can uncover flexible, part-time, and entry opportunities aligned with their skills while building a local network in the Annapolis Valley.
address: 87 Cornwallis Street, Suite 201, Kentville, NS B4N 2E5
solution_text: Spousal Employment Connector: A community-managed job-matching service and skills clinic focused on partners of newcomers, offering resume workshops, local labour-market orientation, short training, and connections to employers open to flexible or part-time roles.

name: Community Connections – Host & Family Match Program
organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
description: ISANS’ Community Connections program matches newcomer individuals and families with volunteer host families and local buddies who provide social support, neighborhood orientation, and informal networking. Matches meet regularly for activities like sharing meals, practicing English, and exploring community resources, helping reduce isolation and accelerating cultural and community integration.
address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1
solution_text: Newcomer Welcome and Buddy Families: Neighbourhood-based buddy or host-family programs that pair newcomers with established residents for social supports, cultural orientation, language practice, and informal networks to reduce isolation.

name: Childminding and Family Drop-in
description: The North Grove is a community hub that provides free childminding during adult programs such as skills-building, community kitchen, and partner-led employment or settlement sessions. Its drop-in family programming and short-term, flexible child care help parents participate in training, appointments, and job search activities, reflecting a community-organized childcare solution.
solution_text: Community Childcare Co-op and Drop-in: A cooperative childcare or drop-in system organized by community groups to provide affordable, flexible childcare during job searches, training, or initial settlement periods.

name: Newcomer Apprenticeship Supports (START and Employer Incentives)
description: The Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency helps internationally trained tradespeople enter paid apprenticeships with local employers by assessing prior learning, supporting credential recognition, and actively matching candidates to apprenticeship opportunities. Through the START program and other employer incentives, NSAA offsets wages and training costs, creating a coordinated pool of paid placements that give newcomers Nova Scotia work experience and a pathway to certification.
solution_text: Local Internship and Apprenticeship Pool: A community-coordinated pool of paid internships, work placements, and apprenticeships with local small businesses and public institutions specifically designated for internationally trained talent to gain local experience.

name: Federal Internship for Newcomers (FIN) – Atlantic Region
description: FIN is a paid internship program that places qualified newcomers into federal departments, agencies, and partner organizations across Atlantic Canada, including Nova Scotia. The program provides Canadian work experience, on-the-job training, and mentorship through time‑limited paid placements, helping internationally trained professionals build local references and transition into long-term employment.
solution_text: Local Internship and Apprenticeship Pool: A community-coordinated pool of paid internships, work placements, and apprenticeships with local small businesses and public institutions specifically designated for internationally trained talent to gain local experience.

name: PARL Events Calendar & Newcomer Outreach
description: Pictou-Antigonish Regional Library (PARL) maintains a regional events calendar featuring conversation cafés, cultural celebrations, arts clubs, and community meetups across its branches. Staff collaborate with settlement agencies and municipalities to promote volunteer roles, local festivals, and sports/recreation groups, providing a centralized, community-run hub that helps newcomers build social networks and a sense of belonging.
solution_text: Social and Cultural Events Calendar: A centralized, community-run calendar and outreach program that promotes multicultural events, volunteer opportunities, sports and arts groups to help newcomers build social ties and a sense of belonging.

name: Refugee Sponsorship Program
organization: Anglican Diocese of Nova Scotia and Prince Edward Island
description: The Anglican Diocese of Nova Scotia and Prince Edward Island acts as a Sponsorship Agreement Holder, equipping parish- and community-based groups to sponsor refugees. Settlement committees in local parishes provide hands-on first‑year support—finding and furnishing housing, registering children in schools, arranging health coverage and appointments, and fostering community connections—functioning as settlement circles that ensure a supported start in Nova Scotia.
solution_text: Community Sponsorship and Settlement Circles: Neighbourhood sponsorship groups that assist with initial settlement needs—housing search, school registration, orientation to services—and provide a local support network through the first year.

name: Volunteer & Peer Leadership Program
description: The North Grove engages newcomers in structured volunteer roles across its community food centre, garden, and family programs, providing on-the-job training, supervision, and reference letters. Participants can progress into peer leader roles with added responsibilities, public-facing experience, and honoraria, creating clear steps from volunteering to paid opportunities on-site or with partner employers. This hands-on pathway helps newcomers build Canadian work experience, local networks, and verified references valued by community employers.
solution_text: Volunteer Work Experience Pathways: Structured volunteer-to-hire programs with local nonprofits and social enterprises that allow newcomers to gain Canadian references, local skills, and visibility within community employers.

name: Cape Breton Connector Program (Employer Inclusion and Newcomer Hiring Pathways)
description: The Cape Breton Connector Program partners with local businesses that commit to inclusive, skills-focused hiring for internationally trained candidates by engaging as Connectors and mentors. The initiative promotes interview flexibility and practical, project-based or short trial placements to evaluate candidates’ skills on the job, helping employers build confidence to make fair, long-term hires.
address: 275 Charlotte Street, Suite 204, Sydney, NS B1P 1C6
solution_text: Business Pledge for Inclusive Hiring: A municipal chamber-led initiative where local businesses commit publicly to fair hiring practices for internationally trained candidates, including interview adjustments, skills-based hiring, and trial work periods.

name: Newcomer Program
description: Futurpreneur’s Newcomer Program provides financing and up to two years of mentorship to immigrants launching businesses in Canada, including small and home-based ventures in Nova Scotia. The program tailors eligibility and support for those new to Canada, pairing participants with local mentors and resources to build networks and navigate the provincial business environment.
address: 1505 Barrington Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5
solution_text: Spousal Entrepreneurship Support: Startup clinics, microgrants, and mentorship for newcomer spouses who want to start home-based or small-scale businesses, run by local economic development and immigrant-serving organizations.

name: YREACH Employer Engagement & Workplace Inclusion Workshops
description: YREACH provides outreach and training to employers across Nova Scotia on hiring, onboarding, and retaining newcomers, including those recruited through the Atlantic Immigration Program. Workshops build cultural competency for HR and supervisors, explain how to interpret international credentials and work histories, and offer practical strategies for inclusive onboarding and day-to-day workplace accommodations.
solution_text: Employer Awareness and Cultural Competency Workshops: Locally delivered training for hiring managers and HR staff on recognizing foreign qualifications, inclusive onboarding, and practical adjustments to integrate internationally trained employees.

name: Intercultural Competence Training for Employers and Community Partners
description: Dalhousie’s International Centre offers customized intercultural competence workshops that help employers and HR professionals build inclusive hiring and onboarding practices for internationally trained employees and co-op students. Training focuses on cross-cultural communication, bias-aware recruitment, team integration, and practical onboarding supports, with guidance on aligning international experience with job competencies.
solution_text: Employer Awareness and Cultural Competency Workshops: Locally delivered training for hiring managers and HR staff on recognizing foreign qualifications, inclusive onboarding, and practical adjustments to integrate internationally trained employees.

name: YREACH (YMCA Settlement Services)
description: YREACH operates province-wide, hosting peer-support circles, newcomer family meet-ups, and community drop-ins in libraries, schools, and YMCA sites, often co-facilitated by staff and volunteer mentors from diverse cultures. Sessions focus on social connection, coping skills, and navigation of services, addressing settlement stress and spousal/family integration while promoting mental well-being.
solution_text: Newcomer Peer Support and Mental Health Groups: Locally available peer-led support groups and culturally sensitive mental health drop-ins to address settlement stressors, isolation, and family integration challenges.

name: Arts Equity Funding Initiative (AEFI)
description: Arts Nova Scotia’s AEFI provides small, accessible project grants to Indigenous, African Nova Scotian, immigrant, deaf and disability, 2SLGBTQIA+, and other equity-deserving artists and collectives. With simplified applications and multiple intakes, it functions as a microgrant stream that can quickly underwrite project costs, short tours/showcases, or gap expenses between gigs—stabilizing artists’ incomes and enabling fast-turnaround community arts activity.
solution_text: Community Arts Microgrant Fund: A locally governed microgrant program funded by municipalities, businesses and community crowdfunding to provide small, fast-turnaround stipends for projects, short tours, or living expenses for artists between gigs.

name: Halifax Public Libraries – Free Community Rooms and Paul O’Regan Hall Bookings
description: Across its branches, Halifax Public Libraries provides free or low-cost meeting rooms, studios, and performance spaces—such as the Paul O’Regan Hall—bookable online by artists and community groups. By opening civic venues during off-peak hours for rehearsals, small performances, and exhibits, the library system functions as a shared-space network that reduces presentation costs and expands access for local creatives.
