solution_text: Shared Venue & Timebank Network: A community-managed scheduling platform that lets venues, churches, schools and businesses share space and off-peak hours with performing and visual artists at low or barter-based cost.

name: St. Andrew’s United Church Halifax – Sanctuary & Hall Rentals for the Arts
description: This downtown church actively shares its acoustically renowned Sanctuary and adjacent halls with choirs, ensembles, festivals, and visual artists at community rates. Its booking office opens non-worship, off-peak hours to cultural uses, providing affordable performance and exhibition space that helps artists present work without prohibitive venue costs.
solution_text: Shared Venue & Timebank Network: A community-managed scheduling platform that lets venues, churches, schools and businesses share space and off-peak hours with performing and visual artists at low or barter-based cost.

name: Mermaid Theatre of Nova Scotia – Touring Productions
description: Mermaid centrally manages routing, trucking of sets/puppets, travel and accommodations, and turnkey marketing kits for its small-scale family productions, enabling efficient multi-stop tours across Nova Scotia and beyond. As the anchor of the Mermaid Imperial Performing Arts Centre in Windsor, it also collaborates with nearby presenters to add neighbouring dates and share logistics, keeping tours affordable for artists and communities.

name: Marigold Cultural Centre – Presenting Series
description: The Marigold co-books with a corridor of North Shore venues to assemble weekend and weeklong tours for small touring productions, aligning dates so artists can play Truro and neighbouring towns on a single run. Staff bundle marketing campaigns, coordinate technical needs, and organize travel and accommodations with partner sites, lowering costs and expanding artists’ reach.
solution_text: Regional Touring Hub and Artist Exchange: Community organizations coordinate a regional touring hub that bundles logistics, marketing and travel for small-scale touring productions so artists can reach neighbouring towns without unsustainable costs.

name: Outdoor Movies in Civic Square
description: Downtown Truro Partnership presents free outdoor movie nights in Civic Square using an inflatable screen and portable A/V, transforming the public plaza into a temporary cinema. These pop-up events often pair with live performances and activations, letting local artists test work and reach new audiences in a low-barrier, highly visible setting.
solution_text: Pop-up & Mobile Venue Program: Organize pop-up performances, galleries and movie nights in parks, storefronts and community centres using portable staging so artists can test work and reach new audiences quickly.

name: NSCAD Community Studio Residency — New Glasgow
organization: NSCAD University (in partnership with Pictou-Antigonish Regional Library)
description: This fixed-term community residency places emerging artists in studio space at the New Glasgow Public Library to create new work and lead public programming. Residents collaborate with the library, local schools, and community partners to deliver workshops, talks, and exhibitions that grow local audiences and education connections. The program provides space, institutional support, and avenues for paid public engagement that stabilize artists’ income and deepen community ties.
address: 182 Dalhousie Street, New Glasgow, NS B2H 5E3
solution_text: Community-led Arts Residency Program: Short paid residencies hosted by libraries, schools, seniors’ homes and cultural centres that give artists income, workspace and opportunities to build local audiences and education partnerships.

name: The Chrysalis Project
description: Neptune’s Chrysalis Project mentors emerging theatre artists through a season-long professional development and creation residency. name: Artist-in-Residence (AIR) Program
description: Lunenburg School of the Arts’ AIR program offers studio facilities, mentorship, and public engagement to selected artists in the UNESCO Old Town of Lunenburg. By providing workspace and community programming alongside public exhibitions and talks, the residency helps artists develop their practice and market presence. The program contributes to cultural tourism and local creative jobs by activating galleries, shops, and hospitality businesses around resident artists’ work.
obstacle_title: Limited availability of high-quality, future-ready jobs
solution_text: Cultural and Creative Sector Supports: Invest in festivals, artist residencies, makers markets, and workspace for artists and cultural entrepreneurs to grow creative industries that boost local screens, music, and tourism jobs.

name: The Bus Stop Theatre Co-op (Affordable Arts Workspace & Festival Hub)
organization: The Bus Stop Theatre Co-operative Limited
description: The Bus Stop Theatre Co-op provides affordable rehearsal and performance space for theatre, music, dance, and screen-related events, and serves as a key venue for festivals like Halifax Fringe and Mayworks. By offering accessible workspace and technical support, it enables artists and creative entrepreneurs to produce shows, earn income, and build audiences. This year-round venue activates the local creative economy by generating gigs for artists, technicians, and producers while drawing patrons to the neighbourhood.
obstacle_title: Limited availability of high-quality, future-ready jobs
solution_text: Cultural and Creative Sector Supports: Invest in festivals, artist residencies, makers markets, and workspace for artists and cultural entrepreneurs to grow creative industries that boost local screens, music, and tourism jobs.

name: Affordable Homeownership with Long-Term Affordability Controls
description: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia acquires land and constructs homes that are sold to qualifying families using ground leases, shared-equity/second-mortgage instruments, and resale restrictions that preserve affordability across owners. This structure separates land value from the home price and embeds lasting affordability conditions—functionally aligning with CLT principles to keep housing permanently affordable while ensuring community-focused stewardship of the asset.
solution_text: Community Land Trust (CLT): Establish a locally governed CLT to buy and hold land for permanently affordable ownership and rental housing, ensuring long-term affordability and community control over development priorities.

name: Backyard and Secondary Suites
description: The Town of Lunenburg allows accessory apartments and detached backyard suites with design guidance that respects the town’s heritage context. The Town provides application forms, checklists, and siting/design guidance, while Development Services staff offer pre-application reviews and permit-navigation support for homeowners. Community information meetings during by-law updates help residents understand how to build compliant, long-term rental ADUs that add to the local housing supply.
solution_text: Accessory Dwelling Units (ADU) Drive: Run community workshops, design guides, and a local permit-navigation service to help homeowners add legal basement suites, laneway houses, and granny flats that expand rental supply quickly and affordably.

name: Public Lands and Assets for Housing (Adaptive Reuse and Redevelopment)
description: Build Nova Scotia inventories surplus and underused public assets and leads partnerships to convert them into housing, including the adaptive reuse of existing buildings. Through calls for proposals and pre-development support, they work with municipalities, post-secondary institutions, non-profits, and private developers to transform vacant or underutilized commercial and institutional properties into mixed-income and student-oriented rentals, backed by feasibility work and capital stack assembly.
address: 1875 Upper Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 1S9
solution_text: Adaptive Reuse of Vacant Buildings: Organize local inventories and partnerships to convert underused commercial, institutional, and industrial spaces into student and mid-market rental units, with community-led feasibility studies and fundraising.

name: HRM Affordable Housing Initiatives and Rapid Housing Conversions
description: Halifax Regional Municipality identifies underused municipal and privately owned sites suitable for housing and supports partners to convert non-residential buildings (e.g., hotels, offices, and institutional spaces) into rental housing through land contributions, expedited approvals, and coordination of federal/provincial funding. These initiatives organize local inventories, enable community-led feasibility studies, and help finance adaptive reuse projects that expand affordable and mid-market rental supply, including options benefitting students.
solution_text: Adaptive Reuse of Vacant Buildings: Organize local inventories and partnerships to convert underused commercial, institutional, and industrial spaces into student and mid-market rental units, with community-led feasibility studies and fundraising.

name: AKOMA Community Development – Former NS Home for Colored Children Redevelopment
description: AKOMA is leading a community-driven redevelopment of the former Nova Scotia Home for Colored Children campus, which includes the adaptive reuse of existing cottages and institutional buildings into affordable and mid-market rental units. The project advances housing supply through partnerships with government and community organizations, detailed feasibility and planning, and active fundraising to deliver culturally grounded, mixed-income housing options.
solution_text: Adaptive Reuse of Vacant Buildings: Organize local inventories and partnerships to convert underused commercial, institutional, and industrial spaces into student and mid-market rental units, with community-led feasibility studies and fundraising.

name: New Dawn Properties – Adaptive Reuse and Mixed-Income Rentals
description: New Dawn repurposes vacant and underused buildings in Sydney and surrounding communities into rental housing and community-serving spaces, emphasizing mixed-income affordability. Their development approach includes community-led feasibility studies, capital fundraising, and partnerships with local institutions and employers to meet demand for student and mid-market rentals while preserving and adapting existing commercial and institutional assets.
solution_text: Adaptive Reuse of Vacant Buildings: Organize local inventories and partnerships to convert underused commercial, institutional, and industrial spaces into student and mid-market rental units, with community-led feasibility studies and fundraising.

name: NSCC Student Housing Initiative
description: Nova Scotia Community College is delivering new and expanded student residences on multiple campuses, co-funded with the Province and local partners to offer quality, mid‑market rental options for students. As a community‑governed public institution, NSCC provides oversight of rents and allocates spaces based on student need, easing pressure on local markets and aligning with a co‑investment model that targets young people.
solution_text: Mid-Market Rental Co-investment: Form local investment consortia (municipalities, employers, credit unions, non-profits) to develop mid-market rental buildings targeted at young professionals and students, with community oversight to set rents and tenancy priorities.

name: Wije’winen Housing (within the Wije’winen Centre)
description: The Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre’s Wije’winen development in Halifax includes a significant number of affordable and mid‑market rental units integrated with cultural, health, and employment services, financed through multi‑partner contributions (municipal, provincial, federal, and philanthropic/social finance). Indigenous‑led community governance ensures transparent oversight of rents and tenant priorities—such as Indigenous youth, students, and early‑career workers—directly aligning with a co‑investment, community‑guided rental model.
solution_text: Mid-Market Rental Co-investment: Form local investment consortia (municipalities, employers, credit unions, non-profits) to develop mid-market rental buildings targeted at young professionals and students, with community oversight to set rents and tenancy priorities.

name: Housing Support and Tenancy Sustainment
description: Welcome Housing & Support Services provides eviction‑prevention and tenancy‑sustainment assistance, including landlord mediation, tenant education, budgeting support, and navigation of benefits like rent supplements. Staff help tenants address arrears by connecting them to emergency financial aid through community partners and negotiating realistic repayment plans—reducing displacement and keeping renting viable for youth and other low‑income renters.
solution_text: Tenant Support and Stabilization Services: Provide community-run tenant information, mediation, legal clinics, and rent-banking to prevent evictions, stabilize households, and make renting safer and more attractive for young people.

name: Build Right Nova Scotia – Habitat for Humanity Volunteer Build Days
organization: Build Right Nova Scotia (Nova Scotia Building Trades / NS Construction Labour Relations Association)
description: Build Right Nova Scotia coordinates union tradespeople and apprentices from member locals to volunteer on Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia build and rehab projects across the province. By supplying skilled volunteer labour and mentoring apprentices on-site, they help renovate existing dwellings when Habitat acquires properties needing repair, accelerating the turnaround of vacant or deteriorated houses into affordable homes.
address: 100 Ilsley Avenue, Unit N, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1L3
solution_text: Vacant-Home Renovation Volunteer Program: Coordinate volunteers, trades apprentices, and local contractors to renovate abandoned or vacant homes for affordable rental or ownership, reducing blight and increasing supply.

name: Housing for All Cape Breton
description: Housing for All Cape Breton is a New Dawn–led initiative that brings residents, community groups, and builders together in working sessions and public forums to push for municipal land-use changes in CBRM that allow gentle density (duplexes, triplexes, and ADUs) and streamline approvals. The coalition prepares recommendations and submissions to Council and planning staff and mobilizes citizen voices to support inclusionary and diverse-housing policies across serviced neighbourhoods.
solution_text: Local Zoning and Policy Advocacy Collective: Form resident-led working groups to advocate for zoning reforms (allowing gentle density, duplexes, triplexes, and ADUs), faster approvals, and inclusionary policies that support diverse housing types.

name: Wolfville Planning Advisory Committee (Housing & Land Use)
description: The Town of Wolfville’s citizen-appointed Planning Advisory Committee functions as a resident-led working group that reviews and recommends zoning and land-use bylaw changes, including town-wide permissions for secondary/garden suites (ADUs), expanded two-unit zones, and reduced barriers to missing-middle infill. By advising Council and leading public consultations, the PAC helps accelerate approvals and embed inclusionary, pro-density policies that expand housing options for students and mid-market renters.
solution_text: Local Zoning and Policy Advocacy Collective: Form resident-led working groups to advocate for zoning reforms (allowing gentle density, duplexes, triplexes, and ADUs), faster approvals, and inclusionary policies that support diverse housing types.

name: Staff Accommodation
description: Keltic Lodge at the Highlands offers employer-managed housing for its workforce, including co‑op students and early‑career hospitality professionals. The lodge sets aside rooms and residences for employees, effectively creating dedicated rental supply and reducing living-cost barriers so new recruits can accept placements within Cape Breton Highlands National Park.
address: 383 Keltic In Road, Ingonish Beach, NS B0C 1L0
solution_text: Employer-Assisted Housing Partnerships: Encourage large local employers (universities, hospitals, employers) to pool land or funding to create rental units or offer rental subsidies/guarantees for early-career staff and students.

name: First-Time Homebuyers Mortgage
description: Sydney Credit Union offers mortgages geared to first-time buyers, enabling small, flexible loans with low down-payment options through mortgage insurance and personalized underwriting. The credit union can combine its lending with programs like the provincial Down Payment Assistance Program or the federal shared-equity incentive to reduce upfront and monthly costs, helping young households access homeownership in Cape Breton and surrounding communities.
solution_text: Micro-mortgage and Community Loan Programs: Work with local credit unions to offer small, flexible mortgages, shared-equity loans, or guarantee schemes tailored to young buyers and renters, lowering barriers to entry into local housing markets.

name: Future Lunenburg – Community Design Workshops
description: Future Lunenburg is the Town’s comprehensive planning and bylaw modernization initiative that employed public design workshops and charrette-style exercises to identify gentle infill opportunities compatible with the community’s UNESCO-designated heritage fabric. Residents helped test ‘missing middle’ housing options—such as accessory suites, duplexes, and courtyard homes—and co-develop design guidelines to ensure new density complements historic streetscapes. The adopted policies expand diverse housing choices with community support, advancing affordability while safeguarding neighbourhood character.
solution_text: Neighborhood Infill Design Charrettes: Host community design sessions to identify context-sensitive 'missing middle' infill opportunities and co-create plans that increase density in ways that local residents support and maintain neighborhood character.

name: Off-Campus Housing
description: Mount Saint Vincent University offers an online off-campus housing resource (linked with Places4Students) that lets landlords advertise rooms, apartments, and shared rentals, and enables students to search by budget, proximity, and amenities. The resource includes sublet listings and directs users to tenant-rights information and community supports, helping young renters secure safe, affordable housing.
solution_text: Housing Matching and Resource Platform: Develop a community-run online platform that matches students, young workers, and landlords for shared rentals, lists affordable units, coordinates sublets, and shares information on tenant rights and supports.

name: Halifax Municipal Archives – Young Canada Works Internships
description: The Halifax Municipal Archives regularly hosts paid student interns—funded through Young Canada Works and other wage-subsidy programs—to digitize, describe, and make accessible municipal records that support community history and civic engagement. The Archives partners with local colleges and universities to recruit students and structure short-term placements that deliver tangible community outcomes (e.g., digitization and public exhibits), directly aligning learning with municipal and community needs.
address: 81 Ilsley Avenue, Unit 11, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1L5
obstacle_title: Skills mismatch and weak work-integrated learning
solution_text: Community-Employer Cooperative Placements: Local businesses, non-profits and municipal programs partner with high schools and colleges to create paid short-term co-op placements focused on community projects (parks, digitization, events). The community helps recruit hosts, subsidizes wages through a pooled fund, and promotes placements to students to increase accessible, locally-relevant work experience.

name: OTCNS Workforce and Skills Initiatives
organization: Ocean Technology Council of Nova Scotia
description: The Ocean Technology Council of Nova Scotia (OTCNS) is an employer-led sector council that works with NSCC, Dalhousie, and training providers to align curricula with ocean-tech workforce needs. Through industry advisory roundtables, working groups, and events, OTCNS surfaces in-demand skills and feeds them back to educators while brokering student internships and project-based placements with member companies. This coordinated, sector-level mechanism improves work-integrated learning and job readiness across Nova Scotia’s ocean industries.
obstacle_title: Skills mismatch and weak work-integrated learning
solution_text: Sector Advisory Councils: Form neighborhood or regional advisory councils of employers, educators, and community reps (health, fisheries, tech, creative industries) that meet quarterly to align curricula, identify in-demand skills, and design local internships or micro-apprenticeships tailored to Nova Scotia’s labour needs.

name: Try-A-Trade Mobile Construction Experience
description: NSCSC’s mobile Try-A-Trade program brings hands-on trade stations and employer partners to communities and coordinates site tours with local contractors and fabrication shops. By letting students and job seekers try tools, meet tradespeople, and observe real workplaces, the initiative provides short, practical exposures that build awareness of construction careers and align training interests with industry needs.
address: 2695 Dutch Village Road, Suite 205, Halifax, NS B3L 4G8
obstacle_title: Skills mismatch and weak work-integrated learning
solution_text: School-to-Work 'Try-It' Days: Coordinate monthly job-shadow and hands-on trade/industry days where local employers open workplaces to students and job seekers for short, low-commitment experiences that build awareness and realistic expectations about local careers.

name: Emera ideaHUB
description: The Emera ideaHUB is Dalhousie’s hardware incubation and prototyping facility that provides machine shop access, electronics benches, and fabrication labs for students and startup teams. Industry mentors and employer partners co-develop real product challenges and support capstone/co-op projects, giving participants applied, work-ready skills aligned with local manufacturing and tech needs.
obstacle_title: Skills mismatch and weak work-integrated learning
solution_text: Community Makerspaces & Simulation Labs: Fund and host local makerspaces or pop-up simulation labs (e.g., hospitality setups, marine tech benches, multimedia studios) where students and local jobseekers can practice applied skills in partnership with employers who help design real-world tasks.

name: Volta Careers (Startup and Scaleup Job Board)
description: Volta’s online careers page lists roles from resident startups and partner companies, including internships, co-ops, part-time, and project-based placements. By centralizing postings from the local innovation community, it provides a practical matching platform that connects students and new grads with hands-on work-integrated learning experiences in Nova Scotia’s tech ecosystem.
address: 1505 Barrington Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5
obstacle_title: Skills mismatch and weak work-integrated learning
solution_text: Local Placement Matching Platform: Develop a simple community-run online platform or bulletin (managed by a chamber or community org) that matches students, recent graduates and adult learners with local co-ops, part-time roles, internships and project-based placements.

name: DeepSense Industry Data Challenges
organization: DeepSense (hosted by Dalhousie University with industry and government partners)
description: DeepSense convenes ocean-sector employers with faculty to translate real company data problems into classroom-ready case datasets, project briefs, and assessment criteria. These employer-authored modules are piloted in Dalhousie and NSCC courses and sprints, giving students hands-on analytics experience on local ocean data while aligning learning outcomes with industry practices and tools.
address: Steele Ocean Sciences Building, 1355 Oxford Street, Halifax, NS B3H 4R2
obstacle_title: Skills mismatch and weak work-integrated learning
solution_text: Employer-Led Curriculum Labs: Host short-term curriculum design sprints where clusters of local employers and instructors co-create modules, case studies and assessment tasks reflecting real local projects, then pilot them in community colleges and high schools.

name: IGNITE Youth & Startup Programming
description: IGNITE Atlantic runs entrepreneurship programming that engages youth and early-stage founders across rural Nova Scotia, connecting them with mentors, business advisors, and prototyping resources. Through bootcamps, workshops, and incubator-style support, participants build companies, access local services, and are connected to small grants and funding competitions—developing practical skills in marketing, finance, and operations while creating community-rooted ventures.
address: 352 East River Road, New Glasgow, NS B2H 3R2
obstacle_title: Skills mismatch and weak work-integrated learning
solution_text: Youth Entrepreneurship Incubators: Run community incubator programs that pair aspiring young entrepreneurs with local mentors, business services and small grants so they build real ventures that create local jobs and teach transferable skills in marketing, finance and operations.

name: Prior Learning Assessment and Recognition (PLAR)
description: MSVU recognizes learning gained through volunteer roles, community leadership, caregiving, and workplace experience by assessing documented portfolios and, where appropriate, challenge exams or interviews. Successful candidates receive transfer credit or course exemptions, and the university engages with local employers and community agencies to ensure assessed competencies align with labour-market and program outcomes.
obstacle_title: Skills mismatch and weak work-integrated learning
solution_text: Community-Based Recognition of Prior Learning: Non-profits and colleges collaborate to assess and formally recognize skills gained through community work, volunteering, informal employment and Indigenous learning, converting experiences into credits, micro-credentials or trade hours to speed job readiness.

name: Learner Housing Program (Clinical Placements)
description: Nova Scotia Health provides free or subsidized short‑term housing in communities across the province for health‑profession students completing clinical placements away from home. The program helps learners accept placements with regional hospitals and clinics by reducing travel and accommodation barriers, and may also offer travel support or mileage reimbursement tied to placement requirements.
address: 7001 Mumford Road, Suite 300, Halifax, NS B3L 2H8
obstacle_title: Skills mismatch and weak work-integrated learning
solution_text: Transport & Housing Supports for Placements: Local governments and community organizations provide targeted supports (transit passes, short-term housing or host-family stipends) to remove logistic barriers that prevent students and apprentices from taking up placements in nearby towns or regional employers.

name: Co-op Access Bursary (Rowe School of Business)
organization: Dalhousie University – Management Career Services (Rowe School of Business)
description: Dalhousie’s Management Career Services offers a Co-op Access Bursary that reduces non-tuition costs that can block students from taking work terms, including relocation, temporary housing, and transportation. By offsetting expenses like bus passes, mileage, and short-term rentals, the fund enables students to pursue placements with employers throughout Nova Scotia.
obstacle_title: Skills mismatch and weak work-integrated learning
solution_text: Transport & Housing Supports for Placements: Local governments and community organizations provide targeted supports (transit passes, short-term housing or host-family stipends) to remove logistic barriers that prevent students and apprentices from taking up placements in nearby towns or regional employers.

name: Co-op Access Bursary
organization: Saint Mary’s University – Co-operative Education Office
description: Saint Mary’s University provides a Co-op Access Bursary to help students cover the extra costs of accepting work terms outside their immediate community, such as transportation and short-term accommodation. This targeted support removes logistical barriers so students can take placements with regional employers across Nova Scotia.
obstacle_title: Skills mismatch and weak work-integrated learning
solution_text: Transport & Housing Supports for Placements: Local governments and community organizations provide targeted supports (transit passes, short-term housing or host-family stipends) to remove logistic barriers that prevent students and apprentices from taking up placements in nearby towns or regional employers.

name: Canada Games Centre – Community Co-working with On-site Child Minding
description: The Canada Games Centre is a Halifax Regional Municipality facility that provides free Wi‑Fi throughout the building, open lounge seating, and rentable meeting rooms that function as accessible co‑working spaces. Its affordable, short‑term child‑minding service lets parents focus on calls, meetings, or laptop work while children are safely cared for nearby. This integrated work‑and‑care setup in a municipal hub supports remote workers, entrepreneurs, and returning young families seeking flexible arrangements.
address: 26 Thomas Raddall Drive, Halifax, NS B3S 0E2
obstacle_title: Youth outmigration and insufficient return pathways
solution_text: Community Co-working & Childcare Hubs: Convert underused municipal spaces into affordable co‑working hubs with reliable broadband and drop‑in childcare to enable remote work, entrepreneurship, and hybrid job arrangements for returning young families.

name: Rath Eastlink Community Centre – Work-Friendly Commons with Child Minding
description: The Rath Eastlink Community Centre provides facility‑wide Wi‑Fi, community lounge areas with tables and power outlets, and bookable rooms that serve as ad hoc co‑working spaces. Its drop‑in child‑minding offering allows parents to concentrate on remote work, meetings, or training sessions while children are cared for on site. This co‑location of broadband-enabled workspace and childcare in a regional civic facility helps entrepreneurs and hybrid workers in Colchester County balance work and family.
obstacle_title: Youth outmigration and insufficient return pathways
solution_text: Community Co-working & Childcare Hubs: Convert underused municipal spaces into affordable co‑working hubs with reliable broadband and drop‑in childcare to enable remote work, entrepreneurship, and hybrid job arrangements for returning young families.

name: MSVU Extended Learning Micro-credentials
organization: Mount Saint Vincent University – Extended Learning
description: Mount Saint Vincent University’s Extended Learning offers short, stackable micro-credentials and digital badges in workforce-relevant topics such as leadership, non-profit management, business communication, and education technology. Created with community and employer input, these offerings provide accessible upskilling pathways that help alumni and early-career professionals align with Nova Scotia’s labour market needs.
obstacle_title: Youth outmigration and insufficient return pathways
solution_text: Skills Bridging & Micro-credential Programs: Work with community colleges and employers to offer short, low-cost micro-credentials and bridging courses aligned with local industry needs so alumni can update skills before returning.

name: Affordable Housing Strategy & Working Group
organization: Municipality of the District of Lunenburg
description: MODL’s Affordable Housing Strategy and cross‑departmental working group coordinate residents, non‑profits, and employers to pilot options like secondary suites, small‑lot/cluster housing, and infill starter units across Lunenburg County. The municipality supports neighbourhood task teams with planning tools, by‑law updates, and partnerships (including with Habitat for Humanity) to bring attainable homes to market for local and returning workers. These initiatives create community‑led pathways to housing that help young people establish themselves locally.
obstacle_title: Youth outmigration and insufficient return pathways
solution_text: Local Housing Solutions Task Group: Form a neighbourhood task group to pilot affordable housing options for young workers and returners — e.g., co‑housing, rent-to-own schemes, and time-limited starter units using community land trusts or partnerships.

name: Newcomers Guide and Welcome Services
description: Halifax Regional Municipality maintains an official Newcomers Guide and online welcome kit that consolidates key relocation information for new and returning residents. The package points to local housing search tools, childcare and school registration, municipal/community event calendars, healthcare access (health cards and family practice registry), and employer networking through the Halifax Partnership Connector Program.
obstacle_title: Youth outmigration and insufficient return pathways
solution_text: Relocation & Welcome Packages: Create standardized community welcome packages for returners that include housing leads, childcare and schooling info, community events calendar, healthcare access details, and employer contacts.

name: Volta DemoCamp and Industry Night Series
description: Volta regularly hosts DemoCamp and Industry Nights where startups and scale-ups demo products, discuss hiring needs, and connect with students, recent grads, and returning professionals. These community pop-ups expose attendees to career paths in Nova Scotia’s tech ecosystem—from co-ops and junior roles to remote-first positions in software, product, and marketing—and enable direct conversations with founders and hiring managers. The showcases help retain and attract young talent by making local and remote opportunities immediately visible and accessible.
address: 1505 Barrington Street, Unit 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5
obstacle_title: Youth outmigration and insufficient return pathways
solution_text: Pop-up Industry Showcases: Host regular local showcases where businesses, cultural groups, and trades demonstrate career paths, apprenticeships, and remote-work roles to alumni and students considering return.

name: Nova Scotia Works Employer Showcases and Job Fairs
description: As a Nova Scotia Works service provider, TEAM Work Cooperative runs recurring pop-up employer showcases, sector information sessions, and multi-employer job fairs at its centre and partner venues. Local businesses, trades, and community organizations demonstrate career pathways, apprenticeships, and remote/hybrid roles to jobseekers, students, and alumni. These events create direct pipelines to employment and apprenticeships that support graduates to stay in or return to Nova Scotia.
address: 7051 Bayers Road, Suite 501, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2
obstacle_title: Youth outmigration and insufficient return pathways
solution_text: Pop-up Industry Showcases: Host regular local showcases where businesses, cultural groups, and trades demonstrate career paths, apprenticeships, and remote-work roles to alumni and students considering return.

name: Acadia Alumni & Students (Ten Thousand Coffees)
description: Acadia University’s Ten Thousand Coffees hub facilitates one-on-one matches between alumni and students for mentorship and networking in the Annapolis Valley. Alumni moving back to Nova Scotia can request local matches with Wolfville-area alumni who act as “returner buddies,” offering introductions, guidance on navigating services and housing, and connections to community and industry events over the first months. The structured, peer-led setup supports practical re-integration and rebuilding of local networks.
obstacle_title: Youth outmigration and insufficient return pathways
solution_text: Peer-led Returner Buddy Program: Match returning alumni with local ‘buddies’ who help with practical re-integration — navigating services, networking, and social connections — for their first 3–6 months back.

name: Communauto Atlantic – Halifax Carshare
description: Communauto Atlantic operates a member‑based carshare network in Halifax that complements public transit and active transportation, giving residents flexible, affordable access to vehicles without the cost of ownership. By strengthening last‑mile options and enabling car‑light living, it helps young professionals and students connect to jobs, co‑working spaces, and services across the region.
obstacle_title: Youth outmigration and insufficient return pathways
solution_text: Transport and Connectivity Improvements: Community-driven campaigns to improve local transit links, ride‑share networks, and last‑mile solutions combined with advocacy for affordable, high-speed home internet to support remote workers.

name: Telehealth Connection Space (Rosa M. Harvey Middleton & Area Library)
description: The Middleton library provides a dedicated, private space with reliable broadband, a computer, camera, and headset for community members to attend virtual health and counseling sessions. Staff help users—particularly teens and young adults—book the room, log into VirtualCareNS or other mental health services, and ensure privacy and tech readiness, mirroring a volunteer telehealth access station model.
obstacle_title: Health and mental health access gaps
solution_text: Volunteer Telehealth Access Stations: Set up private booths in libraries, community centres or youth centres with high-speed internet and staff/volunteer navigators to help youth access telemedicine and virtual mental health appointments.

name: Cape Breton Healthcare Recruitment and Community Navigator
description: The Cape Breton Partnership’s healthcare recruitment initiative supports the attraction and retention of family physicians, nurse practitioners, and allied health professionals by providing a dedicated community navigator who assists with housing searches, school placements, spousal employment, and settlement. Working with local municipalities, businesses, and Nova Scotia Health, they organize welcome packages, community introductions, and mentorship connections to ensure providers and their families are supported and remain in the region.
address: 275 Charlotte Street, Suite 204, Sydney, NS B1P 1C6
obstacle_title: Health and mental health access gaps
solution_text: Local Provider Recruitment and Retention Campaigns: Local businesses, municipalities and community groups coordinate sign-on bonuses, housing supports, mentorship, and community welcome packages to attract and retain family physicians, nurse practitioners and counsellors.

name: Recruitment Antigonish (Physician Recruitment and Retention)
organization: Recruitment Antigonish (St. Martha’s Regional Hospital Foundation)
description: Recruitment Antigonish coordinates with community partners to attract and retain family physicians and other primary care providers, offering personalized community tours, welcome packages, and spousal/settlement support including housing and school navigation. The program partners with Nova Scotia Health to align sign-on and relocation incentives and pairs new clinicians with local mentors and hospital leaders to build lasting ties to the community.
obstacle_title: Health and mental health access gaps
solution_text: Local Provider Recruitment and Retention Campaigns: Local businesses, municipalities and community groups coordinate sign-on bonuses, housing supports, mentorship, and community welcome packages to attract and retain family physicians, nurse practitioners and counsellors.

name: Mental Health Counselling
description: The Youth Project offers free counselling for 2SLGBTQIA+ youth, reducing cost barriers to timely mental health support. Services are sustained through community donations, grants, and fundraising, effectively operating as a community-managed subsidy that makes short-term counselling accessible when private therapy is unaffordable.
obstacle_title: Health and mental health access gaps
solution_text: Community-run Sliding-scale Counselling Fund: Establish a community-managed fund (supported by donations, municipal grants, and fundraisers) to subsidize short-term counselling for youth who face cost barriers to private therapy.

name: Counselling and Support Services
description: Every Woman’s Centre provides free, confidential counselling and support to women and girls, including youth, eliminating cost as a barrier to accessing short-term mental health care. Services are supported by grants, community donations, and fundraising, which together operate as a community-managed subsidy in place of private therapy fees.
obstacle_title: Health and mental health access gaps
solution_text: Community-run Sliding-scale Counselling Fund: Establish a community-managed fund (supported by donations, municipal grants, and fundraisers) to subsidize short-term counselling for youth who face cost barriers to private therapy.

name: Youth Health Centres
description: Nova Scotia Health’s school-based Youth Health Centres provide confidential, youth-friendly navigation to health and mental health services across the province. Coordinators help students book appointments, complete referrals and consent/intake forms, and coordinate follow-up with families and providers. They also advocate within schools and the health system to reduce barriers and prevent drop-offs from care.
address: 7 Mellor Avenue, Unit 5, Dartmouth, NS B3B 0E8
obstacle_title: Health and mental health access gaps
solution_text: Youth Navigation and Peer Advocacy Program: Train youth navigators and peer advocates to help peers schedule appointments, complete intake forms, follow up on care, and advocate with providers and schools to reduce drop-offs from the care pathway.

name: 211 Nova Scotia – Online Community and Social Services Directory
description: 211 Nova Scotia maintains a continuously updated, searchable online directory of community and government services across the province, including primary care options, youth mental health services, crisis lines, and peer supports. The listings include how to access services, eligibility criteria, hours, and language availability, and the service is accessible online and via 24/7 phone/text to help residents navigate local resources.
obstacle_title: Health and mental health access gaps

Employer advisory input and ongoing supervisor evaluations inform program outcomes and technical curricula, while co‑op coordinators align job-ready skills with local demand. Graduates build direct pathways into full-time roles—often with the same employers—benefiting from documented salary bands and clear early-career progression after co‑op.

By broadcasting in-depth, locally produced stories about entrepreneurs, skilled tradespeople, and standout employers across TV, radio, and digital, the show creates positive narratives about real career pathways and sector momentum in the province. Community, industry, and education partners regularly work with CBC producers to surface story leads, aligning closely with the goal of using local media to highlight strengths and opportunity.

name: Downtown Sydney Pop-Up Shops
organization: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design

name: The Loaded Ladle (Student‑Run Food Co‑op)

obstacle_title: Community Amenities and Vibrant Public Spaces

name: Friday Night Market (Annapolis Royal)
description: From late spring through fall, the Town of Annapolis Royal hosts a weekly Friday Night Market that turns St. George Street and Market Square into a pedestrian-friendly evening marketplace. Local artisans, food vendors, and shops stay open late while live music and street performances create a safe, family-friendly ‘night out’ experience that supports downtown businesses and social gathering.

name: Community Wheels
organization: St. Margaret’s Bay Community Transportation Society
description: Community Wheels is a volunteer-driven, door-to-door community transit service serving the rural St. Margaret’s Bay area. Riders can pre-book subsidized trips for medical, shopping, and social/recreational activities, including evening events, and drivers provide door-to-door assistance that functions as a safe escort for seniors and youth. By filling gaps in limited public transit after hours, it enables residents to attend community programming and reduces isolation in smaller communities.

name: NSWiFi Public Wi‑Fi Program
description: Build Nova Scotia operates the NSWiFi network that provides free public Wi‑Fi in high-traffic public spaces across the province, including along the Halifax and Lunenburg waterfronts and other community hubs. In tandem with its waterfront stewardship, the organization also invests in public-realm upgrades—weather‑resistant seating, lighting, bike racks, and power—making plazas and boardwalks comfortable, safe, and usable for longer hours and seasons.

name: Argyle & Grafton Shared Streetscape
description: Halifax Regional Municipality redesigned Argyle and Grafton Streets into a pedestrian‑priority public space with integrated seating, widened sidewalks, programmable and safety lighting, bike racks, and power for events—supporting nightlife and all‑season use. name: Nova Scotia Health – Summer Student Employment Program

name: Continuing Care Recruitment & Retention Services

As a community-run hub, it coordinates childminding at varied times and connects families with local childcare options, easing access for those working or training in sectors with nonstandard schedules. obstacle_title: Workforce Shortages in Care, Construction, and Skilled Trades

name: SMU Alumni Insurance Program (Home, Auto & Tenant)
description: Saint Mary’s University Alumni Association partners with a national insurer to provide alumni in Nova Scotia with affinity group rates on home, tenant, and auto insurance, helping graduates manage cost-of-living pressures. The alumni office periodically coordinates broker/advisor info sessions and webinars so members can compare policies, understand coverage trade-offs, and get claims guidance.
obstacle_title: Cost of Living Pressures Beyond Housing
solution_text: Group Insurance Pools and Broker Clinics: Local associations (youth chambers, co-ops, freelancer networks) negotiate group rates for auto, renter's and small-business insurance; host clinics with brokers to compare low-cost coverage and claims advice.

name: Family Home Child Care (FHCC) Program
description: The YMCA’s licensed Family Home Child Care program recruits, trains, and supports approved home child care providers and matches them with families seeking small-group care. By enabling multiple families to share a single caregiver in a home setting and to arrange part‑time or non‑standard hours, the network lowers per‑family costs and offers flexible, community‑based options that align with cooperative and shared childminding models for working parents.
obstacle_title: Cost of Living Pressures Beyond Housing
solution_text: Cooperative Childcare and Shared Nanny Networks: Parent-run childcare co-ops, shared nanny/childminding networks and time-share childcare arrangements that lower childcare costs and increase flexible, community-based options for working young parents.

name: The Spark Zone (Nova Scotia Sandbox)
organization: Saint Mary’s University – The Spark Zone Sandbox
description: The Spark Zone is a university-led incubator that provides free co-working space, mentorship, workshops, and small seed funding to help students and recent graduates validate ideas and build early-stage ventures. By covering essentials like workspace, coaching, and prototype micro-grants, it reduces startup costs and risk for emerging entrepreneurs.
obstacle_title: Cost of Living Pressures Beyond Housing
solution_text: Micro-Grants, Incubators and Co‑Working for Young Entrepreneurs: Community-managed micro-grants, low-cost co-working spaces, equipment libraries and mentorship programs that reduce startup costs for small businesses and side hustles.

name: Student Line of Credit and Youth Accounts
description: Sydney Credit Union provides a Student Line of Credit with competitive rates and interest-only payments while in school, helping students and young workers finance tuition, tools, and training with lower monthly costs. It also offers youth-friendly chequing and savings options with low or no monthly fees, plus digital banking tools and in-branch advice to build financial skills. Together, these products make day-to-day banking more affordable and provide accessible credit to manage rising non-housing living costs.
obstacle_title: Cost of Living Pressures Beyond Housing
solution_text: Community Credit Union Programs and Matched-Savings: Partnerships with local credit unions to offer no-fee accounts, low-interest small loans, matched-savings programs for training or emergencies, and youth-friendly financial products.

name: Repair Café (Alderney Gate Public Library – Dartmouth)
description: At Alderney Gate Public Library, volunteers with skills in sewing, electronics, and small repairs offer their time to help neighbours troubleshoot and fix broken items. The skill-sharing format functions like a community time exchange—participants receive service and learn skills without fees, reducing everyday costs and strengthening peer-to-peer support.
obstacle_title: Cost of Living Pressures Beyond Housing
solution_text: Time Banks and Skill-Swap Platforms: Local time-banking systems where residents exchange hours of work (childcare, tutoring, repairs) instead of money, building mutual aid networks that cut service costs for young people.

name: Income Tax Preparation Program
description: Parker Street Food & Furniture Bank runs a free income tax preparation program for low-income individuals and families, ensuring clients file accurately and access refundable credits and benefits. The organization also provides drop-in support to review bills and budgets and connects people with subsidies and partner agencies for debt counselling to help stabilize household finances.
obstacle_title: Cost of Living Pressures Beyond Housing
solution_text: Financial Literacy, Benefits Navigation and Tax Clinics: Regular community workshops and drop-in clinics that teach budgeting, debt management, claims for provincial/federal benefits, and how to access eligible subsidies to improve net income.

name: Community Food Centre Market and Pantry
description: The North Grove runs community food access programs that include an affordable market and a pantry-style distribution of donated and rescued foods like produce and bread. Working with local grocers, farms, and provincial food recovery partners, they redistribute surplus foods to Dartmouth North residents. These programs help reduce grocery bills for families and young people while cutting down on food waste.
obstacle_title: Cost of Living Pressures Beyond Housing
solution_text: Community Fridges and Food Rescue Partnerships: Neighbourhood fridges, pantry nodes and partnerships with grocery stores, restaurants and campuses to redistribute surplus food to residents, reducing household grocery expense and waste.

name: Advocacy
description: Feed Nova Scotia’s advocacy program compiles data and stories from people accessing food support across the province to highlight how food, transportation, and utility costs strain household budgets. Using this lived‑experience evidence, they engage municipal and provincial leaders to push for income‑based solutions—like living‑wage policies, stronger income assistance, and affordable access programs—that reduce cost‑of‑living pressures beyond housing.
obstacle_title: Cost of Living Pressures Beyond Housing
solution_text: Advocacy Network for Local Cost-of-Living Policies: A community-led coalition that collects lived-experience data and advocates municipal/provincial leaders for targeted supports (transit passes, childcare subsidies, living-wage bylaws), amplifying community-driven policy wins.

name: Poverty Solutions Advisory Committee
description: This United Way Halifax initiative brings together people with lived and living experience of poverty to identify barriers—such as transit fares, childcare costs, and low wages—and co‑develop policy recommendations. The committee engages directly with HRM and Nova Scotia decision‑makers to advocate for targeted supports (e.g., affordable transit programs and childcare subsidies), ensuring community‑driven insights shape local policy change.
obstacle_title: Cost of Living Pressures Beyond Housing
solution_text: Advocacy Network for Local Cost-of-Living Policies: A community-led coalition that collects lived-experience data and advocates municipal/provincial leaders for targeted supports (transit passes, childcare subsidies, living-wage bylaws), amplifying community-driven policy wins.
